MTHROP.overview: MTHROP defines the return-to-idle threshold above the learned minimum closed-throttle position. After an engine has been driven off-idle, releasing the accelerator pedal causes throttle position sensor voltage to drop back toward the mechanical stop. In factory calibrations, MTHROP is set to one count, representing approximately zero point zero two zero volts above the learned closed-throttle baseline. Throttle voltage must fall below the sum of minimum learned throttle plus MTHROP before the engine controller clears the off-idle flag and re-engages closed-loop idle speed regulation and idle spark advance feedback.
MTHROP.overview_markdown:
`MTHROP` defines the return-to-idle threshold above the learned minimum closed-throttle position.

After an engine has been driven off-idle, releasing the accelerator pedal causes throttle position sensor voltage to drop back toward the mechanical stop. In factory calibrations, `MTHROP` is set to one count, representing approximately zero point zero two zero volts above the learned closed-throttle baseline. Throttle voltage must fall below the sum of minimum learned throttle plus `MTHROP` before the engine controller clears the off-idle flag and re-engages closed-loop idle speed regulation and idle spark advance feedback.
MTHROP.tuners_guide: MTHROP is critical for vehicles with aging throttle linkages, weak return springs, or slight throttle shaft friction. If an aftermarket or worn throttle body sticks slightly upon closing—stopping zero point zero three to zero point zero five volts above the learned mechanical stop—the engine controller will never detect return-to-idle, leaving the engine idling high without closed-loop idle spark or idle air stepper motor control. Increasing MTHROP to two or three counts ensures the controller reliably detects closed throttle even if the physical linkage has minor resting position variation.
MTHROP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Sticky Throttle Recovery**:
  * If weak return springs or thermal expansion prevent the throttle blade from returning to within 0.02V of the stop, increasing `MTHROP` to two or three counts cures hanging idle.
* **Return-to-Idle Deadband**:
  * Because `MTHROP` (1 count) is lower than `MTHRCL` (2 counts), the system creates a 1-count hysteresis preventing idle flutter.
* **Idle Control Re-Engagement**:
  * Clearing the off-idle flag re-activates closed-loop AIS stepper motor control and idle spark advance stabilization.
* **Factory Default**:
  * Set to one count (~0.020 Volts) in stock calibrations.

MXSBST.overview: MXSBST defines the upper boundary for allowable turbocharger boost pressure as a function of road vehicle speed. Because turbocharged front-wheel-drive vehicles easily break traction and induce severe wheel spin or torque steer in first and second gears, Chrysler engineers incorporated speed-dependent boost limits into the controller. At low vehicle speeds (such as 0 to 25 mph), the table can limit boost to moderate levels, smoothly elevating the ceiling to full boost as vehicle speed climbs and available tire grip increases at higher speeds.
MXSBST.overview_markdown:
`MXSBST` defines the upper boundary for allowable turbocharger boost pressure as a function of road vehicle speed.

Because turbocharged front-wheel-drive vehicles easily break traction and induce severe wheel spin or torque steer in first and second gears, Chrysler engineers incorporated speed-dependent boost limits into the controller. At low vehicle speeds (such as 0 to 25 mph), the table can limit boost to moderate levels, smoothly elevating the ceiling to full boost as vehicle speed climbs and available tire grip increases at higher speeds.
MXSBST.tuners_guide: Functions as a simple and effective boost-by-speed traction management tool. On high-horsepower street cars running street radial tires, lowering the low-speed table entries (0 to 30 mph) to 7 to 10 psi prevents blown-off front tires upon initial launch and roll-ons, while ramping to 18 to 25 psi above 50 mph when aerodynamics and vehicle inertia provide sufficient tire loading. On dedicated drag cars equipped with slicks and a prepped surface where immediate maximum launch traction is available, tuners set all points in this table to maximum target boost to ensure no speed-based restriction impedes acceleration.
MXSBST.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Boost-by-Speed Traction Control**:
  * Restricts boost in low-speed operating regions to control wheelspin in 1st and 2nd gears on front-wheel-drive platforms.
  * Ramp boost progressively from 8 psi at 0 to 20 mph up to full target boost above 50 mph.
* **Drag Racing Configuration**:
  * If running slicks on a prepped track, max out all table entries (set to 29.4 psi) to ensure immediate full boost in every gear.
* **Speed Sensor Scaling**:
  * Road speed input is derived from the transmission distance sensor (`VehicleSpeed_HB`); ensure speed sensor calibration is accurate.
* **Running Minimum Priority**:
  * Evaluated as the fifth table in `GetBoostTargetFromTables`; lower values will clamp `Temp4` downward.

* **Execution Frequency**: Evaluated every main program loop pass.
* **Input Variable**: Pointer loaded with `#MXSBST_AllowedBoost_FromSpeed` (line 9448). `VehicleSpeed_HB` loaded into accumulator D and shifted left three times (`asld`, lines 9450-9452) to scale road speed.
* **Evaluation**: Evaluated via `bsr LookupAndKeepSmallerBoostGoal` (line 9453), updating `Temp4` if speed limits boost.

	asld		    ; shift left (d=d*2)

NBOFFS.overview: NBOFFS provides a fine-tuning voltage offset added to the simulated narrowband oxygen sensor voltage in the wideband conversion routine. During closed-loop fueling, the engine controller continuously trims injector pulse width to oscillate sensor voltage across a fixed 0.45-volt switching threshold. By adding a calibrated positive or negative voltage offset to the simulated sensor signal, NBOFFS shifts the effective closed-loop target air-fuel ratio richer or leaner without requiring modification of the main AFR2NB transfer curve. The factory setting of 128 counts represents zero voltage offset.
NBOFFS.overview_markdown:
`NBOFFS` provides a fine-tuning voltage offset added to the simulated narrowband oxygen sensor voltage in the wideband conversion routine.

During closed-loop fueling, the engine controller continuously trims injector pulse width to oscillate sensor voltage across a fixed 0.45-volt switching threshold. By adding a calibrated positive or negative voltage offset to the simulated sensor signal, `NBOFFS` shifts the effective closed-loop target air-fuel ratio richer or leaner without requiring modification of the main `AFR2NB` transfer curve.

The factory setting of 128 counts represents zero voltage offset.
NBOFFS.tuners_guide: Use NBOFFS to bias closed-loop cruising air-fuel ratio richer or leaner without altering transfer function tables. Raising NBOFFS above 128 adds voltage, making the controller perceive a richer mixture and driving closed-loop fueling leaner (e.g., 15.2:1 AFR for improved highway fuel efficiency). NO2RET.overview: NO2RET defines the amount of ignition timing retard applied when the nitrous oxide activation switch is triggered. Burning nitrous oxide releases concentrated oxygen into the combustion chamber, accelerating the flame front and causing cylinder pressure to peak much earlier than normal. To protect pistons, connecting rods, and head gaskets from extreme cylinder pressure spikes, ignition timing must be retarded whenever nitrous flows. NO2RET provides this dedicated safety retard, with the factory setting of 31 counts providing approximately 3.875 degrees of spark retard.
NO2RET.overview_markdown:
`NO2RET` defines the amount of ignition timing retard applied when the nitrous oxide activation switch is triggered.

Burning nitrous oxide releases concentrated oxygen into the combustion chamber, accelerating the flame front and causing cylinder pressure to peak much earlier than normal. To protect pistons, connecting rods, and head gaskets from extreme cylinder pressure spikes, ignition timing must be retarded whenever nitrous flows.

`NO2RET` provides this dedicated safety retard, with the factory setting of 31 counts providing approximately 3.875 degrees of spark retard.
NO2RET.tuners_guide: Calibrate NO2RET according to the size of your nitrous shot. A general automotive tuning rule of thumb is approximately 1.5 to 2.0 degrees of timing retard for every 50 horsepower of nitrous flow. For a 50 hp shot, calibrate NO2RET for roughly 2.0 degrees retard (16 counts). For a 100 hp shot, use 4.0 degrees retard (32 counts). For a 150 hp shot, use 6.0 degrees retard (48 counts). Always inspect spark plug ground straps for heat marks and monitor knock sensor retard when dialing in nitrous timing on a dyno. The factory setting provides approximately 3.875 degrees retard, suitable for an initial 75 to 100 hp nitrous shot.
NO2RET.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Shot Size Scaling**: A standard tuning rule of thumb is 1.5 to 2.0 degrees of retard for every 50 horsepower of nitrous shot.
* **Recommended Setpoints**: 16 counts (~2.0 degrees) for 50 hp, 32 counts (~4.0 degrees) for 100 hp, and 48 counts (~6.0 degrees) for 150 hp.
* **Combined Boost Caution**: When spraying nitrous on top of turbocharger boost, use conservative timing retard and inspect spark plug ground straps for signs of excessive combustion heat.

* Result is stored in RAM variable `NO2Retard` at line 10364.
* In `CalculateSparkAdvance_MM` at line 8006, instruction `suba NO2Retard` subtracts the retard directly from total spark advance.

NO2SWS.overview: NO2SWS selects the digital input switch bitmask that signals nitrous oxide activation to the engine controller. When nitrous oxide is sprayed into an engine, cylinder combustion pressure and flame speed rise sharply, requiring instantaneous ignition timing retard to prevent severe detonation. NO2SWS links a hardware input (such as a wide-open throttle switch, nitrous arming switch, or relay trigger) to the controller's nitrous timing retard routine. When the selected switch activates, the controller immediately subtracts the retard angle defined by NO2RET from total spark advance.
NO2SWS.overview_markdown:
`NO2SWS` selects the digital input switch bitmask that signals nitrous oxide activation to the engine controller.

When nitrous oxide is sprayed into an engine, cylinder combustion pressure and flame speed rise sharply, requiring instantaneous ignition timing retard to prevent severe detonation. `NO2SWS` links a hardware input (such as a wide-open throttle switch, nitrous arming switch, or relay trigger) to the controller's nitrous timing retard routine.

When the selected switch activates, the controller immediately subtracts the retard angle defined by `NO2RET` from total spark advance.
NO2SWS.tuners_guide: Select the digital input switch bitmask that corresponds to your nitrous system wiring. Common choices include Speed Control On/Off or Set switch, Brake Switch, or Air Conditioning Switch. Polarity is determined by option flag opt_NO2Pol in configuration options: if your switch grounds the input when active, configure the polarity flag for active-low operation; if it supplies 12 volts, configure for active-high. Always test switch operation with the nitrous bottle closed by datalogging NO2Retard in MPScan to ensure timing retard activates only when the nitrous system triggers.

* **Polarity Configuration**: Toggle `opt_NO2Pol` in `OPTN1` to match switch polarity (active-low ground signal vs. active-high 12V signal).
* **Safety Testing**: Datalog `NO2Retard` in MPScan with the engine off to verify that the retard value activates when the nitrous switch engages and clears when released.

O2HIGH.overview: O2HIGH defines the upper voltage threshold required for immediate validation of the narrowband oxygen sensor signal during the closed-loop entry sequence. When cold, a zirconium oxygen sensor has very high internal electrical impedance and generates an inert mid-range voltage. Once the sensor heats up and begins generating an active voltage swing above O2HIGH, the engine controller confirms the sensor is fully operational and immediately enables closed loop without waiting for delay timers. In stock calibrations, O2HIGH is set to 38 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.74 volts.
O2HIGH.overview_markdown:
`O2HIGH` defines the upper voltage threshold required for immediate validation of the narrowband oxygen sensor signal during the closed-loop entry sequence.

When cold, a zirconium oxygen sensor has very high internal electrical impedance and generates an inert mid-range voltage. Once the sensor heats up and begins generating an active voltage swing above `O2HIGH`, the engine controller confirms the sensor is fully operational and immediately enables closed loop without waiting for delay timers.

In stock calibrations, `O2HIGH` is set to 38 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.74 volts.
O2HIGH.tuners_guide: Raising O2HIGH requires the oxygen sensor to generate a higher rich voltage peak before it is recognized as active, which can help reject noisy signals from unheated single-wire sensors on cold mornings. Lowering O2HIGH accelerates closed-loop entry by accepting lower voltage peaks as proof of sensor activity, which is beneficial when utilizing modern heated four-wire sensors that reach operating temperature quickly. Setting O2HIGH too high can delay closed-loop operation if exhaust cooling at idle prevents the sensor from reaching high voltage swings.
O2HIGH.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Heated Sensor Upgrades**:
  * When converting to a heated 4-wire oxygen sensor, lowering `O2HIGH` slightly allows faster closed-loop engagement after cold starts.
* **Signal Noise Immunity**:
  * On unheated single-wire setups, keeping `O2HIGH` at 38 counts (0.74V) prevents electrical ground noise from prematurely triggering closed loop.
* **Setting Too High**:
  * If set above 0.85V, cool idle exhaust temperatures may prevent the sensor from ever satisfying immediate closed-loop entry.

O2HSWP.overview: O2HSWP establishes the rich switching threshold for closed-loop oxygen sensor feedback. During closed-loop operation, the engine controller monitors sensor voltage against this threshold: when sensor voltage equals or exceeds O2HSWP, the mixture is recognized as rich, triggering the primary ramp logic to begin subtracting fuel. In stock calibrations, O2HSWP is set to 25 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.49 volts, positioned directly at the steep stoichiometric curve of a narrowband zirconium sensor.
O2HSWP.overview_markdown:
`O2HSWP` establishes the rich switching threshold for closed-loop oxygen sensor feedback.

During closed-loop operation, the engine controller monitors sensor voltage against this threshold: when sensor voltage equals or exceeds `O2HSWP`, the mixture is recognized as rich, triggering the primary ramp logic to begin subtracting fuel.

In stock calibrations, `O2HSWP` is set to 25 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.49 volts, positioned directly at the steep stoichiometric curve of a narrowband zirconium sensor.
O2HSWP.tuners_guide: Adjusting O2HSWP allows tuners to subtly shift the closed-loop target air-fuel ratio. Raising O2HSWP requires the sensor to reach a higher voltage before recognizing a rich mixture, which biases the average closed-loop air-fuel ratio slightly richer, improving combustion smoothness on engines with large cams. Lowering O2HSWP makes the controller switch lean sooner, slightly leaning out the closed-loop center. Ensure that O2HSWP remains higher than O2LSWP to maintain the switching hysteresis deadband.
O2HSWP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Rich Bias Tuning**:
  * Raising `O2HSWP` to 26-28 counts biases the closed-loop stoichiometric oscillation slightly richer (approx 14.5:1), stabilizing idle on performance cams.
* **Lean Bias Tuning**:
  * Lowering `O2HSWP` brings the switching point closer to 0.45V, centering fuel delivery strictly at 14.7:1.
* **Deadband Maintenance**:
  * Must be strictly greater than `O2LSWP` to maintain switching hysteresis.

O2ITIM.overview: O2ITIM defines the duration that closed-loop oxygen sensor feedback is inhibited when transitioning from a rich idle state back to standard closed-throttle closed-loop operation. During specific idle diagnostic routines, such as setting basic ignition distributor timing or calibrating minimum throttle plate airflow opening via a diagnostic scan tool, the engine controller commands deliberate rich open-loop fueling for combustion stability. When these test routines finish, residual fuel vapors in the intake manifold and cylinder ports require time to clear. O2ITIM provides a calibrated delay timer that prevents the oxygen sensor from prematurely trying to lean out the mixture, ensuring a smooth transition back to stoichiometric closed-loop control without engine surging. In factory calibrations, O2ITIM is set to 255 counts.
O2ITIM.overview_markdown:
`O2ITIM` defines the duration that closed-loop oxygen sensor feedback is inhibited when transitioning from a rich idle state back to standard closed-throttle closed-loop operation.

During specific idle diagnostic routines, such as setting basic ignition distributor timing or calibrating minimum throttle plate airflow opening via a diagnostic scan tool, the engine controller commands deliberate rich open-loop fueling for combustion stability. When these test routines finish, residual fuel vapors in the intake manifold and cylinder ports require time to clear.

`O2ITIM` provides a calibrated delay timer that prevents the oxygen sensor from prematurely trying to lean out the mixture, ensuring a smooth transition back to stoichiometric closed-loop control without engine surging. In factory calibrations, `O2ITIM` is set to 255 counts.
O2ITIM.tuners_guide: Tuning O2ITIM helps prevent idle hunting and lean stumbling when returning to closed loop after idle diagnostic modes or rich idle stabilization periods. Lowering O2ITIM shortens the transition hold duration, which allows the oxygen sensor to take control of idle fueling more rapidly after throttle blips or service procedures. Raising O2ITIM extends the open-loop delay, giving vehicles with long-duration camshafts and sluggish intake airspeed additional time to stabilize combustion before closed-loop feedback responds. Setting this value to zero eliminates the post-rich-idle inhibit delay entirely, immediately enabling closed-loop evaluation as soon as off-idle flags clear.
O2ITIM.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Idle Stability Tuning**:
  * Lengthening the delay by raising `O2ITIM` helps prevent idle hunting on cammed engines with low intake vacuum when returning from rich idle conditions.
* **Lowering the Value**:
  * Commands the engine controller to re-engage closed-loop stoichiometric feedback more quickly after idle diagnostic testing or throttle closures.
* **Zeroing Out**:
  * Disables the delay timer completely, immediately restoring closed loop once test flags clear.
* **Diagnostic Relevance**:
  * Active specifically after disengaging basic timing lock mode (coolant sensor disconnect or scan tool command).

* **Enclosing Subroutine**: `DealWithSpecialIdle_SetBasicTiming_MM` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:5813-5838`), instruction line 5828.

  * Closed throttle confirmed (`BitFlags_4f` bit `b4f_OffIdle` clear).
  * Rich idle enrichment timer active (`Timer_OffThrottleFuelEnrich` nonzero) transitioning to zero.

O2ITIM.raw_text: OVERVIEW: O2ITIM defines the duration that closed-loop oxygen sensor feedback is inhibited when transitioning from a rich idle state back to standard closed-throttle closed-loop operation. During specific idle diagnostic routines, such as setting basic ignition distributor timing or calibrating minimum throttle plate airflow opening via a diagnostic scan tool, the engine controller commands deliberate rich open-loop fueling for combustion stability. When these test routines finish, residual fuel vapors in the intake manifold and cylinder ports require time to clear. O2ITIM provides a calibrated delay timer that prevents the oxygen sensor from prematurely trying to lean out the mixture, ensuring a smooth transition back to stoichiometric closed-loop control without engine surging. In factory calibrations, O2ITIM is set to 255 counts. | TUNER'S GUIDE: Tuning O2ITIM helps prevent idle hunting and lean stumbling when returning to closed loop after idle diagnostic modes or rich idle stabilization periods. Lowering O2ITIM shortens the transition hold duration, which allows the oxygen sensor to take control of idle fueling more rapidly after throttle blips or service procedures. Raising O2ITIM extends the open-loop delay, giving vehicles with long-duration camshafts and sluggish intake airspeed additional time to stabilize combustion before closed-loop feedback responds. Setting this value to zero eliminates the post-rich-idle inhibit delay entirely, immediately enabling closed-loop evaluation as soon as off-idle flags clear.

O2LIMH.overview: O2LIMH defines the absolute maximum positive fuel trim limit for short-term oxygen sensor feedback. During closed-loop operation, the feedback counter accumulates primary and secondary ramp kicks to correct for lean conditions. O2LIMH acts as a hard upper clamp, preventing the short-term feedback counter from adding more fuel than calibrated. In stock calibrations, O2LIMH is set to 127 counts, corresponding to approximately +24.8 percent maximum fuel enrichment above the current base and adaptive fueling calculation.
O2LIMH.overview_markdown:
`O2LIMH` defines the absolute maximum positive fuel trim limit for short-term oxygen sensor feedback.

During closed-loop operation, the feedback counter accumulates primary and secondary ramp kicks to correct for lean conditions. `O2LIMH` acts as a hard upper clamp, preventing the short-term feedback counter from adding more fuel than calibrated.

In stock calibrations, `O2LIMH` is set to 127 counts, corresponding to approximately +24.8 percent maximum fuel enrichment above the current base and adaptive fueling calculation.
O2LIMH.tuners_guide: Constraining O2LIMH prevents the oxygen sensor from heavily over-fueling the engine during transient lean spikes or misfires. On high-performance engines with large fuel injectors, a full +24.8 percent fuel addition can deliver excessive fuel, causing plug fouling or catalytic converter overheating; lowering O2LIMH to 50 or 60 counts caps short-term enrichment at approximately +10 to +12 percent. Setting O2LIMH to zero prevents short-term feedback from ever adding fuel, clamping the controller to lean-only corrections.
O2LIMH.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Capping Positive STFT**:
  * Clamping `O2LIMH` to 50-60 counts limits maximum short-term enrichment to +10% to +12%, protecting against plug fouling.
* **Large Injector Tuning**:
  * Large injectors deliver massive fuel volume per tick; reducing `O2LIMH` prevents over-enrichment during transient lean toggles.
* **Mathematical Authority**:
  * Factory 127 counts represents +24.8% maximum fuel enrichment (127 / 512).

O2LIML.overview: O2LIML defines the absolute minimum negative fuel trim limit for short-term oxygen sensor feedback. When the oxygen sensor detects a rich mixture, the controller decrements the feedback counter to remove fuel. O2LIML provides a hard lower clamp, preventing the controller from subtracting more fuel than calibrated. In stock calibrations, O2LIML is set to signed -77 counts (stored as 179 unsigned), which corresponds to approximately -15.0 percent maximum fuel reduction. This prevents a failing sensor from dangerously leaning out the engine.
O2LIML.overview_markdown:
`O2LIML` defines the absolute minimum negative fuel trim limit for short-term oxygen sensor feedback.

When the oxygen sensor detects a rich mixture, the controller decrements the feedback counter to remove fuel. `O2LIML` provides a hard lower clamp, preventing the controller from subtracting more fuel than calibrated.

O2LIML.tuners_guide: Raising O2LIML toward zero narrows the allowable short-term leanout authority, protecting modified engines against excessive leaning during tuning or road operation. For engines with aggressive camshafts that misfire slightly at idle, raw fuel in the exhaust can fool the oxygen sensor into reporting a rich condition; setting O2LIML to -25 counts (-5 percent) prevents the controller from pulling excessive fuel and causing an idle stall. Setting O2LIML to zero completely blocks short-term fuel reduction.

* **Preventing False Leanout**:

* **Mathematical Authority**:
  * Factory signed -77 counts represents -15.0% maximum fuel reduction (-77 / 512).

O2LOW.overview: O2LOW defines the lower voltage threshold for immediate validation of the narrowband oxygen sensor signal. If the sensor produces a clear lean reading below O2LOW during warmup, the controller knows the sensor has reached operating temperature and is capable of full amplitude swings. The controller immediately validates the sensor flag without waiting for delay timers. In stock calibrations, O2LOW is set to 15 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.29 volts.
O2LOW.overview_markdown:
`O2LOW` defines the lower voltage threshold for immediate validation of the narrowband oxygen sensor signal.

If the sensor produces a clear lean reading below `O2LOW` during warmup, the controller knows the sensor has reached operating temperature and is capable of full amplitude swings. The controller immediately validates the sensor flag without waiting for delay timers.

In stock calibrations, `O2LOW` is set to 15 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.29 volts.
O2LOW.tuners_guide: Raising O2LOW allows higher lean voltages to qualify as immediate sensor validation, which speeds up closed-loop entry after cold starts on engines with good exhaust heat retention. Lowering O2LOW requires the sensor to pull down to a deeper lean voltage before immediate validation is granted, ensuring that only fully heated sensors enter closed loop without timer delays. Setting O2LOW too low can cause extended open-loop operation if sensor ground offsets prevent the signal from dropping below the threshold.
O2LOW.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Lean Signal Validation**:
  * Any signal below `O2LOW` (approx 0.29V) proves the sensor is hot and swinging lean, immediately triggering closed loop.
* **Ground Offset Mitigation**:
  * If wiring resistance creates a ground voltage offset, raising `O2LOW` to 18-20 counts (0.35-0.39V) prevents delayed closed-loop entry.
* **Interaction with O2HIGH**:
  * Together, `O2LOW` and `O2HIGH` define the active boundaries outside the intermediate warmup zone.

O2LSWP.overview: O2LSWP defines the lean switching threshold for closed-loop oxygen sensor feedback. When sensor voltage falls below O2LSWP, the mixture is classified as lean, instructing the controller to apply rich ramp kicks to add fuel. In factory calibrations, O2LSWP is set to 24 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.47 volts. The difference between O2LSWP (24 counts) and O2HSWP (25 counts) forms a 1-count hysteresis deadband that prevents electrical noise from causing rapid toggle chatter when voltage passes through the center.
O2LSWP.overview_markdown:
`O2LSWP` defines the lean switching threshold for closed-loop oxygen sensor feedback.

When sensor voltage falls below `O2LSWP`, the mixture is classified as lean, instructing the controller to apply rich ramp kicks to add fuel. In factory calibrations, `O2LSWP` is set to 24 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.47 volts.

The difference between `O2LSWP` (24 counts) and `O2HSWP` (25 counts) forms a 1-count hysteresis deadband that prevents electrical noise from causing rapid toggle chatter when voltage passes through the center.
O2LSWP.tuners_guide: Shifting O2LSWP works in tandem with O2HSWP to define the closed-loop switching window. Raising O2LSWP biases the closed-loop average richer, while lowering O2LSWP biases it leaner. Expanding the separation between O2LSWP and O2HSWP by lowering O2LSWP to 22 or 23 counts widens the hysteresis deadband, which eliminates false toggles on setups with electrical noise or ungrounded oxygen sensor bungs. Setting O2LSWP equal to or higher than O2HSWP eliminates the deadband and causes toggle instability.
O2LSWP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Hysteresis Widening**:
  * Lowering `O2LSWP` to 22-23 counts (0.43-0.45V) widens the deadband against `O2HSWP`, filtering electrical noise from single-wire sensors.
* **Centering Stoichiometric Point**:
  * Calibrated to 0.47V, immediately below the steep slope of the narrowband sensor voltage curve.
* **Polarity Requirement**:
  * Must be strictly less than `O2HSWP` (`O2LSWP < O2HSWP`).

O2MIDH.overview: O2MIDH defines the upper voltage limit of the stuck-in-the-middle diagnostic zone for active closed-loop operation. A healthy narrowband oxygen sensor constantly swings between rich (above 0.6V) and lean (below 0.3V). If the sensor voltage remains trapped between O2MIDL and O2MIDH, it indicates that the sensor is cold, poisoned, unplugged, or suffering from a high-resistance wiring fault. In factory calibrations, O2MIDH is set to 28 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.55 volts. If the signal remains in this middle zone, the controller increments a fault timer toward clearing adaptive memory and setting diagnostic codes.
O2MIDH.overview_markdown:
`O2MIDH` defines the upper voltage limit of the stuck-in-the-middle diagnostic zone for active closed-loop operation.

A healthy narrowband oxygen sensor constantly swings between rich (above 0.6V) and lean (below 0.3V). If the sensor voltage remains trapped between `O2MIDL` and `O2MIDH`, it indicates that the sensor is cold, poisoned, unplugged, or suffering from a high-resistance wiring fault.

In factory calibrations, `O2MIDH` is set to 28 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.55 volts. If the signal remains in this middle zone, the controller increments a fault timer toward clearing adaptive memory and setting diagnostic codes.
O2MIDH.tuners_guide: Widening the middle band by raising O2MIDH makes the stuck-sensor detection logic more aggressive, catching sluggish or aged sensors that fail to swing cleanly into rich voltage territory. Narrowing the middle band by lowering O2MIDH helps prevent false fault triggers on vehicles with high-flow exhaust systems where rapid exhaust cooling at idle can momentarily dampen sensor voltage swings. Keep O2MIDH higher than the switching threshold O2HSWP.
O2MIDH.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Stuck Sensor Diagnostics**:
  * Defines the upper edge (0.55V) of the inactive sensor detection zone.
* **Idle Exhaust Cooling**:
  * If free-flowing exhaust causes sensor cooling at idle that dampens voltage swings, lowering `O2MIDH` slightly prevents false fault timers.
* **Switching Threshold Hierarchy**:
  * Must be maintained higher than `O2HSWP` (0.49V) to preserve normal switching.

A healthy narrowband oxygen sensor constantly swings between rich (above 0.6V) and lean (below 0.3V). If the sensor voltage remains trapped between O2MIDL and O2MIDH, it indicates that the sensor is cold, poisoned, unplugged, or suffering from a high-resistance wiring fault. O2MIDL.overview: O2MIDL establishes the lower voltage limit of the stuck-in-the-middle diagnostic zone during closed-loop operation. Operating continuously inside this zone triggers adaptive memory erasure and leads to fault code generation.

O2TIME.overview: O2TIME defines the delay time required to validate the oxygen sensor when its output voltage is hovering in the intermediate warmup band between O2TLML and O2TLMH. Rather than forcing immediate closed loop or staying in open loop indefinitely, the engine controller increments a qualification timer against O2TIME. Once this duration elapses, the sensor is accepted as valid and closed loop is engaged. In stock calibrations, O2TIME is set to 7 counts, representing approximately 19.6 seconds of cumulative intermediate signal verification.
O2TIME.overview_markdown:
`O2TIME` defines the delay time required to validate the oxygen sensor when its output voltage is hovering in the intermediate warmup band between `O2TLML` and `O2TLMH`.

Rather than forcing immediate closed loop or staying in open loop indefinitely, the engine controller increments a qualification timer against `O2TIME`. Once this duration elapses, the sensor is accepted as valid and closed loop is engaged.

In stock calibrations, `O2TIME` is set to 7 counts, representing approximately 19.6 seconds of cumulative intermediate signal verification.
O2TIME.tuners_guide: Adjusting O2TIME controls how conservatively the ECU qualifies a warming oxygen sensor. Raising O2TIME increases the required verification delay, preventing premature closed-loop entry if an unheated oxygen sensor is slow to reach operating temperature in high-flow tubular exhaust manifolds. Lowering O2TIME reduces the verification period, allowing faster closed-loop engagement when running modern high-wattage heated oxygen sensors. Setting O2TIME to zero allows immediate closed-loop entry once the sensor enters the warmup band.
O2TIME.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Sensor Warmup Verification**:
  * Controls verification delay (7 counts ≈ 19.6 seconds) when O2 signal hovers in the intermediate warmup zone.
* **Heated Sensor Conversion**:
  * Lowering `O2TIME` to 2-3 counts allows fast closed-loop engagement with 4-wire heated sensors.
* **Tubular Headers**:
  * Lengthening `O2TIME` prevents premature closed-loop entry if unheated sensors take longer to warm up in tubular exhaust manifolds.

O2TLMH.overview: O2TLMH establishes the upper boundary of the delayed closed-loop entry voltage band. If the oxygen sensor voltage is not high enough to exceed O2HIGH for immediate closed-loop entry, but falls between O2TLML and O2TLMH, the sensor is demonstrating partial activity as it warms up. The controller marks this condition and starts the delayed qualification timer O2TIME rather than locking out closed loop completely. In factory calibrations, O2TLMH is set to 31 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.61 volts.
O2TLMH.overview_markdown:
`O2TLMH` establishes the upper boundary of the delayed closed-loop entry voltage band.

If the oxygen sensor voltage is not high enough to exceed `O2HIGH` for immediate closed-loop entry, but falls between `O2TLML` and `O2TLMH`, the sensor is demonstrating partial activity as it warms up. The controller marks this condition and starts the delayed qualification timer `O2TIME` rather than locking out closed loop completely.

In factory calibrations, `O2TLMH` is set to 31 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.61 volts.
O2TLMH.tuners_guide: Adjusting O2TLMH modifies the sensitivity of the warmup qualification window. Raising O2TLMH expands the delayed entry band, permitting the controller to initiate the timed qualification sequence across a broader voltage range during sensor warmup. Lowering O2TLMH narrows the band, requiring the sensor to generate higher voltage before timed qualification can begin. This parameter rarely requires adjustment unless troubleshooting slow closed-loop transitions with relocated or ceramic-coated exhaust manifolds.
O2TLMH.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Warmup Window Upper Edge**:
  * Defines the upper limit of the delayed qualification zone (0.61V).
* **Relocated Sensor Troubleshooting**:
  * On downpipe-mounted sensors with slower warmup, raising `O2TLMH` allows the qualification countdown to begin earlier.
* **Relationship to O2HIGH**:
  * Must be maintained strictly lower than `O2HIGH`.

O2TLML.overview: O2TLML defines the lower boundary of the delayed closed-loop entry voltage band. When the engine controller is evaluating whether the oxygen sensor has warmed up sufficiently to begin closed-loop operation, sensor voltage between O2TLML and O2TLMH indicates the sensor is generating partial output. In stock calibrations, O2TLML is set to 15 counts, corresponding to approximately 0.29 volts. Signals falling inside this band initiate the delayed entry countdown rather than being rejected outright.

`O2TLML` defines the lower boundary of the delayed closed-loop entry voltage band.

When the engine controller is evaluating whether the oxygen sensor has warmed up sufficiently to begin closed-loop operation, sensor voltage between `O2TLML` and `O2TLMH` indicates the sensor is generating partial output. O2TLML.tuners_guide: Modifying O2TLML alters the lower threshold of the warmup qualification window. Raising O2TLML requires the sensor to produce a higher voltage before the delayed qualification timer can start, which prevents noisy cold sensor signals from triggering early closed-loop entry. Lowering O2TLML allows the controller to recognize weak early sensor activity sooner. On vehicles converted to modern heated oxygen sensors, this parameter typically performs flawlessly at the factory setting.

* **Warmup Window Lower Edge**:

* **Heated Sensor Conversion**:
  * Modern heated sensors stabilize quickly, making factory 0.29V calibration ideal.
* **Interaction with O2LOW**:

OCTAE.overview: OCTAE defines the artificial manifold pressure delta step injected during off-idle throttle transitions. When the driver steps on the accelerator pedal and the throttle blade opens, intake manifold pressure rises rapidly. Because physical pressure sensor filtering introduces a brief mathematical lag in the running average manifold pressure variable, the engine controller subtracts OCTAE from instantaneous manifold pressure when leaving idle. This subtraction artificially suppresses the historical average pressure baseline, creating an instantaneous positive delta pressure jump that triggers immediate transient fuel enrichment and responsive ignition advance before the physical sensor filter catches up. Factory calibrations configure OCTAE to two counts, representing approximately zero point two three psi.
OCTAE.overview_markdown:
`OCTAE` defines the artificial manifold pressure delta step injected during off-idle throttle transitions.

When the driver steps on the accelerator pedal and the throttle blade opens, intake manifold pressure rises rapidly. Because physical pressure sensor filtering introduces a brief mathematical lag in the running average manifold pressure variable, the engine controller subtracts `OCTAE` from instantaneous manifold pressure when leaving idle. This subtraction artificially suppresses the historical average pressure baseline, creating an instantaneous positive delta pressure jump that triggers immediate transient fuel enrichment and responsive ignition advance before the physical sensor filter catches up. Factory calibrations configure `OCTAE` to two counts, representing approximately zero point two three psi.
OCTAE.tuners_guide: Adjusting OCTAE tailors the sharpness of off-idle throttle response. Raising OCTAE forces a larger artificial pressure differential upon tip-in, prompting the fuel system to inject a heavier burst of acceleration enrichment. If an engine suffers from a momentary lean stumble or hesitation just as the throttle opens from a stop, increasing OCTAE to three or four counts can eliminate the hesitation. Conversely, on engines fitted with very large aftermarket fuel injectors, an excessive tip-in step can cause over-fueling and black smoke; lowering OCTAE toward zero or one count softens the initial transient fuel burst for smoother low-speed driving.
OCTAE.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Tip-In Hesitation Cure**:
  * Increasing `OCTAE` to three or four counts forces a sharper delta manifold pressure step, curing light off-idle lean stumbles.
* **Large Fuel Injector Tuning**:
  * On engines with oversized injectors, lowering `OCTAE` softens off-idle transient fuel delivery to prevent rich bogging.
* **Clamped Lower Floor**:
  * If the subtraction of `OCTAE` would reduce average pressure below minimum thresholds, `MINAMP` enforces a hard lower boundary.
* **Factory Setting**:
  * Set to two counts (approx 0.23 psi) in factory 2.5L calibrations.

OFFPER.overview: OFFPER defines the percentage proportion of the off-idle air conditioning airflow adder ACCTBL that is instantly retracted when the compressor clutch disengages. While driving off-idle with the air conditioner on, ACCTBL injects auxiliary bypass airflow to counteract compressor drag during coast-down. When the compressor clutch disengages, compressor drag vanishes immediately. If the full off-idle air offset were allowed to decay away slowly, the vehicle would continue to coast forward with diminished engine braking, feeling like the throttle is hanging open. OFFPER dictates what percentage of the ACCTBL airflow adder is instantly subtracted from the stepper motor position at the exact moment the clutch disengages. In factory calibrations, OFFPER is set to 192 counts, commanding an instantaneous retraction of exactly 75 percent (192/256) of the A/C airflow adder.
OFFPER.overview_markdown:
`OFFPER` defines the percentage proportion of the off-idle air conditioning airflow adder `ACCTBL` that is instantly retracted when the compressor clutch disengages.

While driving off-idle with the air conditioner on, `ACCTBL` injects auxiliary bypass airflow to counteract compressor drag during coast-down. When the compressor clutch disengages, compressor drag vanishes immediately.

If the full off-idle air offset were allowed to decay away slowly, the vehicle would continue to coast forward with diminished engine braking, feeling like the throttle is hanging open.

`OFFPER` dictates what percentage of the `ACCTBL` airflow adder is instantly subtracted from the stepper motor position at the exact moment the clutch disengages.

In factory calibrations, `OFFPER` is set to 192 counts, commanding an instantaneous retraction of exactly 75 percent (192/256) of the A/C airflow adder.
OFFPER.tuners_guide: OFFPER controls deceleration feel when the air conditioning compressor turns off while coasting down from speed. OPTN1.overview: OPTN1 is the first custom feature configuration register introduced in the Turbonator codebase to unlock advanced performance enhancements. Configured in factory baseline files to sixteen counts, OPTN1 provides software toggles that allow tuners to enable or disable custom features without recompiling the assembly source code. The switches in OPTN1 govern switchable dual-stage boost control, boost switch input electrical polarity, flashing the dashboard check engine light upon knock detection, nitrous oxide ignition retard activation, and nitrous switch polarity. When these options are enabled, the firmware activates dedicated routines to monitor external switches and modify engine operations in real time.
OPTN1.overview_markdown:
`OPTN1` is the first custom feature configuration register introduced in the Turbonator codebase to unlock advanced performance enhancements.

Configured in factory baseline files to sixteen counts, `OPTN1` provides software toggles that allow tuners to enable or disable custom features without recompiling the assembly source code. The switches in `OPTN1` govern switchable dual-stage boost control, boost switch input electrical polarity, flashing the dashboard check engine light upon knock detection, nitrous oxide ignition retard activation, and nitrous switch polarity. When these options are enabled, the firmware activates dedicated routines to monitor external switches and modify engine operations in real time.
OPTN1.tuners_guide: Tuners configure OPTN1 in MPTune to suit street, drag, and track applications. Enabling switchable boost allows drivers to alternate between a conservative low-boost daily setting and full target boost using a physical toggle switch on the dashboard. If the boost switch logic works backward, toggling the boost switch polarity bit flips whether an open or closed switch commands high boost. Enabling the flash check engine on knock option provides real-time visual detonation warnings by pulsing the check engine light whenever cylinder retard is applied. Enabling nitrous retard applies a pre-calibrated ignition timing retard whenever the nitrous activation switch is engaged, protecting against excessive cylinder pressures.
OPTN1.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Switchable Dual-Stage Boost**:
  * Set the switchable boost enable bit to activate dual boost levels, toggling between low wastegate boost and full target boost via an external dashboard switch.
* **Boost Switch Polarity**:
  * Toggle the boost switch polarity bit if the physical switch is normally closed rather than normally open.
* **Knock Alert Check Engine Light**:
  * Enabling the flash check engine on knock bit pulses the dashboard warning lamp whenever individual cylinder retard is active, providing immediate visual feedback of combustion knock.
* **Nitrous Timing Retard**:
  * Enable nitrous retard and set nitrous switch polarity to apply instant ignition retard when nitrous solenoids fire.

  * Bit 1 (`opt_SwBstPol`, 0x02): Boost switch polarity select.
  * Bit 4 (`opt_FlashCE`, 0x10): Flash check engine light on knock enable.
  * Bit 5 (`opt_NO2Pol`, 0x20): Nitrous switch polarity select.
  * Bit 6 (`opt_NO2Retard`, 0x40): Nitrous ignition retard enable.
* **Branch Execution**:
  * In `CheckBoostSwitch`, `bita #opt_SwBoost` branches to `StoreBoostTarget` if disabled, bypassing switch evaluation.

	bita #opt_SwBstPol ; check the switch polarity
	beq  Polarity_Lo

	bitb BSTSWS_HighBoostSwitchSelect
	beq  LoadLoBoostAndLookup	    ; branch if equal (zero)
	bra  StoreBoostTarget

Polarity_Lo:
	bitb BSTSWS_HighBoostSwitchSelect
	bne  LoadLoBoostAndLookup	    ; branch if not equal (not zero)
	bra  StoreBoostTarget

OPTN2.overview: OPTN2 serves as the second custom feature configuration register in the Turbonator codebase, controlling rev limiter mechanics, launch control, turbocharger anti-lag, boost algorithms, and wideband oxygen sensor emulation. In factory baseline files, OPTN2 is configured to five counts, enabling spark-based rev limiting and two-step launch control. Unlike factory firmware that solely cut fuel during over-rev conditions, OPTN2 provides independent toggles for spark cut and fuel cut rev limiting. It also enables stationary drag racing launch control, bang-bang exhaust pop, launch spark retard, second-generation proportional wastegate duty cycle logic, and wideband-to-narrowband oxygen sensor conversion.
OPTN2.overview_markdown:
`OPTN2` serves as the second custom feature configuration register in the Turbonator codebase, controlling rev limiter mechanics, launch control, turbocharger anti-lag, boost algorithms, and wideband oxygen sensor emulation.

In factory baseline files, `OPTN2` is configured to five counts, enabling spark-based rev limiting and two-step launch control. Unlike factory firmware that solely cut fuel during over-rev conditions, `OPTN2` provides independent toggles for spark cut and fuel cut rev limiting. It also enables stationary drag racing launch control, bang-bang exhaust pop, launch spark retard, second-generation proportional wastegate duty cycle logic, and wideband-to-narrowband oxygen sensor conversion.
OPTN2.tuners_guide: OPTN2 gives tuners unprecedented flexibility for race and performance calibrations. Selecting spark-based rev limiting produces rapid, consistent rev control that builds turbocharger boost on the staging line without the severe lean backfires associated with fuel-only limiters. Enabling launch control activates a stationary two-step rev limiter below a set vehicle speed, allowing consistent drag strip launches. Selecting the second-generation boost control algorithm upgrades wastegate management to proportional-integral closed-loop logic with adaptive airflow correction. When using an aftermarket wideband oxygen sensor controller, enabling wideband-to-narrowband conversion translates the zero-to-five-volt wideband signal into simulated narrowband voltages for closed-loop cruising while logging actual air-fuel ratio.
OPTN2.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Spark Cut vs Fuel Cut Limiters**:
  * Bit 0 enables spark-based rev limiting, while Bit 1 enables fuel-based limiting. Running spark cut alone provides crisper staging limiter operation and rapid boost building on the two-step.
* **Stationary Launch Control (Two-Step)**:
  * Enabling Bit 2 engages the launch control routine when vehicle speed is below the launch speed threshold, holding engine speed at the launch setpoint.
* **Anti-Lag & Bang-Bang Options**:
  * Bit 3 enables bang-bang spark cut patterns and Bit 5 enables anti-lag timing retards to spool large turbochargers.
* **Second-Generation Boost Control**:
  * Bit 6 switches the boost solenoid algorithm from early duty cycle logic to advanced proportional wastegate control.
* **Wideband to Narrowband Conversion**:
  * Bit 7 enables live transfer function lookup that converts wideband input voltages into simulated narrowband signals.

* **Bitmask Decoding**:

  * Bit 1 (`opt_FuelRevLim`, 0x02): Fuel-based rev limiter enable.
  * Bit 2 (`opt_StageLim`, 0x04): Launch control / staging limiter enable.
  * Bit 3 (`opt_BangBang`, 0x08): Bang-bang spark pattern enable.
  * Bit 5 (`opt_AntiLag`, 0x20): Anti-lag spark retard enable.
  * Bit 6 (`opt_T2BC`, 0x40): Second-generation boost control enable.
  * Bit 7 (`opt_WB2NB`, 0x80): Wideband to narrowband conversion enable.

PEFTBL.overview: PEFTBL defines the engine pumping efficiency (volumetric efficiency) curve versus engine speed (RPM) in Chrysler speed-density calibrations. Speed-density fuel calculation estimates mass airflow based on intake manifold pressure, displacement, charge air temperature, and the mechanical breathing ability of the engine across the RPM range. PEFTBL scales base fuel pulsewidth across the entire operating range from idle to 8160 RPM to match cylinder head port airflow, camshaft lift and duration, and intake manifold runner resonance. In Turbonator SMEC v19, the firmware utilizes the proven stock 0 to 99.6 percent volumetric efficiency scaling routine.
PEFTBL.overview_markdown:
`PEFTBL` defines the engine pumping efficiency (volumetric efficiency) curve versus engine speed (RPM) in Chrysler speed-density calibrations.

Speed-density fuel calculation estimates mass airflow based on intake manifold pressure, displacement, charge air temperature, and the mechanical breathing ability of the engine across the RPM range. `PEFTBL` scales base fuel pulsewidth across the entire operating range from idle to 8160 RPM to match cylinder head port airflow, camshaft lift and duration, and intake manifold runner resonance.

In Turbonator SMEC v19, the firmware utilizes the proven stock 0 to 99.6 percent volumetric efficiency scaling routine.
PEFTBL.tuners_guide: PEFTBL is the primary volumetric efficiency shaping tool when upgrading camshafts, porting cylinder heads, installing larger valves, or fitting high-flow intake manifolds. When a performance camshaft shifts peak torque and volumetric efficiency higher in the RPM band, PEFTBL values must be raised at mid-to-high RPM (3500 to 6500 RPM) and lowered at low RPM (1500 to 2500 RPM) to match actual cylinder filling. Raising PEFTBL values increases fueling across all throttle modes at that specific engine speed. Lowering PEFTBL values leans out fueling at that RPM point without altering manifold pressure break points. Because Turbonator SMEC v19 retains stock 100 percent scaling, values represent 0 to 99.6 percent volumetric efficiency.
PEFTBL.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Performance Camshaft Profiling**:
  * Reshape `PEFTBL` to match the engine's new volumetric efficiency curve when installing aftermarket camshafts (e.g. Taft, FWD-P, or custom grinds).
* **RPM-Specific Fuel Shaping**:
  * Raise values where cylinder filling improves (peak torque and upper mid-range); lower values at low RPM if a large cam causes low-speed airflow reversion.
* **Universal Fueling Effect**:
  * Modifies part-throttle, wide-open throttle, and idle fueling equally at each RPM point because volumetric efficiency is an engine airflow physical property.
* **SMEC v19 Scaling Architecture**:
  * Turbonator SMEC v19 re-adopted the stock 0 to 99.6 percent volumetric efficiency routine (experimental 150% scaling code is commented out in assembly).
PEFTBL.operating_conditions:
* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `IncludePumpEff` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:6187-6204`), instruction line 6192.
* **Gating Conditions**:
  * Executed in `CalculateSumOfAllFuelModifiers_MM` for every running engine calculation pass.
  * Evaluates `EngineRpm_HB` (engine speed high byte).
* **Scaling Math**:
  * Looked up via `Lookup4ByteTable`, then scales `Temp0` via `ScaleYbyA`, storing the resulting modifier in `SumOfFuelModifiers_HB`.

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In `CalculateSumOfAllFuelModifiers_MM`, execution enters `IncludePumpEff` at line 6187. Line 6189 executes `jsr ScaleXbyB_addingA_intoD`, saving the modifier product into `Temp0`. Line 6191 loads `ldaa EngineRpm_HB`, and line 6192 loads `ldx #PEFTBL_PumpingEfficiency`. `Lookup4ByteTable` interpolates the volumetric efficiency percentage. At line 6195, `beq LAC5B` checks if efficiency is zero. If non-zero, `ldY Temp0` and `jsr ScaleYbyA` scale the modifier word, storing the final result into `SumOfFuelModifiers_HB` at line 6198.

; --- IncludePumpEff (T-SMEC_v19.asm:6187-6203) ---
IncludePumpEff:
        asrb        ; Arithmetic shift right
	jsr  ScaleXbyB_addingA_intoD	; call subroutine
	stD *Temp0
	ldaa EngineRpm_HB    ; load a with memory contents
	ldx  #PEFTBL_PumpingEfficiency	  ; load index with value
	jsr  Lookup4ByteTable	 ; call subroutine
; stock PEFTBL Code - only use with stock peftbl template!!!
        beq  LAC5B          ; branch if equal (zero)
        ldY  Temp0	    ; store D to RAM
        jsr  ScaleYbyA      ; call subroutine
        stY SumOfFuelModifiers_HB    ; store Y index
        rts                 ; return from subroutine

LAC5B:  ldd  Temp0          ; load d (a&b) with memory contents
        stD *SumOfFuelModifiers_HB    ; store D to RAM
        rts                 ; return from subroutine

PEFTBL.calibration_notes:
* **Firmware Architecture**: As documented in the assembly comments at line 6194, v19 reverted to the stock `ScaleYbyA` PEFTBL routine, with experimental 150% code commented out.
* **10-Point Curve**: 10-point interpolation curve spanning 0 to 8160 RPM.
* **Output Variable**: Stores final cumulative fuel modifier into 16-bit RAM variable `SumOfFuelModifiers_HB`.

PEFTBL.raw_text: OVERVIEW: PEFTBL defines the engine pumping efficiency (volumetric efficiency) curve versus engine speed (RPM) in Chrysler speed-density calibrations. Speed-density fuel calculation estimates mass airflow based on intake manifold pressure, displacement, charge air temperature, and the mechanical breathing ability of the engine across the RPM range. PEFTBL scales base fuel pulsewidth across the entire operating range from idle to 8160 RPM to match cylinder head port airflow, camshaft lift and duration, and intake manifold runner resonance. In Turbonator SMEC v19, the firmware utilizes the proven stock 0 to 99.6 percent volumetric efficiency scaling routine. | TUNER'S GUIDE: PEFTBL is the primary volumetric efficiency shaping tool when upgrading camshafts, porting cylinder heads, installing larger valves, or fitting high-flow intake manifolds. When a performance camshaft shifts peak torque and volumetric efficiency higher in the RPM band, PEFTBL values must be raised at mid-to-high RPM (3500 to 6500 RPM) and lowered at low RPM (1500 to 2500 RPM) to match actual cylinder filling. Raising PEFTBL values increases fueling across all throttle modes at that specific engine speed. Lowering PEFTBL values leans out fueling at that RPM point without altering manifold pressure break points. Because Turbonator SMEC v19 retains stock 100 percent scaling, values represent 0 to 99.6 percent volumetric efficiency.

PERKCK.overview: PERKCK defines the scaling percentage multiplier applied to the off-idle air conditioning airflow adder ACCTBL. Depending on whether the air conditioning system is transitioning between active states or operating in steady-state off-idle cruising, the full airflow step offset looked up from ACCTBL may need to be scaled down. PERKCK acts as a global proportioning scalar applied to the raw speed-dependent steps retrieved from ACCTBL. In factory calibrations, PERKCK is set to 192 counts, representing an airflow scaling factor of exactly 75 percent (192/256).
PERKCK.overview_markdown:
`PERKCK` defines the scaling percentage multiplier applied to the off-idle air conditioning airflow adder `ACCTBL`.

Depending on whether the air conditioning system is transitioning between active states or operating in steady-state off-idle cruising, the full airflow step offset looked up from `ACCTBL` may need to be scaled down. PERKCK acts as a global proportioning scalar applied to the raw speed-dependent steps retrieved from `ACCTBL`.

In factory calibrations, `PERKCK` is set to 192 counts, representing an airflow scaling factor of exactly 75 percent (192/256).
PERKCK.tuners_guide: PERKCK provides a simple master scalar to increase or decrease off-idle air conditioning airflow across all vehicle speeds without modifying the individual points in ACCTBL. If your vehicle needs slightly more decel dashpot air with the A/C running across the entire speed spectrum, raising PERKCK from 192 (75%) up to 230 or 255 (90% to 100%) scales up the entire curve proportionally. Conversely, if off-idle A/C airflow is generally too generous across all cruising speeds, lowering PERKCK to 128 (50%) reduces total A/C dashpot air proportionally.
PERKCK.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Global Scaling of ACCTBL**:
  * Adjust `PERKCK` to scale overall off-idle A/C airflow up or down without reshaping the individual speed breakpoints in `ACCTBL`.
* **Increasing Dashpot Air**:
  * Raise `PERKCK` to 220 to 255 counts (86% to 100%) to provide stronger overall anti-stall dashpot air with the A/C on.
* **Linear Percentage Multiplier**:
  * 255 counts represents 100% full scale; factory setting of 192 counts represents 75%.
PERKCK.operating_conditions:
* **Enclosing Routine**: `HandleAcCutout` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:2170-2465`) within `CalculateTargetIdleSpeedAndAisPosition_MM`.
* **Gating Conditions**:
  * Runs immediately after `ACCTBL` lookup at line 2459.
  * Flag `b2e_bit2` tested at line 2460.
  * Loads `PERKCK` into accumulator A at line 2461 and executes `mul` against accumulator B.
  * The high product byte in accumulator B becomes the final scaled A/C airflow adder.

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In `CalculateTargetIdleSpeedAndAisPosition_MM`, line 2459 fetches raw steps from `ACCTBL` into accumulator A. Line 2461 executes `ldaa PERKCK_AcClutchAisAdjustmentConstant`. Line 2462 executes `mul` (multiplying `ACCTBL` by `PERKCK`). Line 2463 adds carry (`adca #0x00`) to round the 16-bit product. Line 2464 executes `tab` to move the high-order result into accumulator B, which is then added to the base position in accumulator A at line 2466 (`aba`).
technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
; --- HandleAcCutout (T-SMEC_v19.asm:2460-2465) ---
	brclr *BitFlags_2e, #b2e_bit2, L1147	; branch if bit(s) clear
	ldaa PERKCK_AcClutchAisAdjustmentConstant    ; load a with memory contents (data is c0)
	mul		    ; multiply (d=a*b)
	adca #0x00	    ;  -00000000-
	tab		    ; b = a
L1147:	ldaa Temp4	    ; load a with memory contents

PERKCK.calibration_notes:
* **Scaling**: 192 counts = 192 / 256 = 0.75 (75%).
* **Companion Parameter**: Direct scaling multiplier for `ACCTBL`.
* **Factory Value**: 0xC0 (192 counts).

PIAMSK.overview: PIAMSK defines the diagnostic output driver circuit mask for Port A of the Peripheral Interface Adapter. In Chrysler SMEC engine controllers, high-current inductive drivers and relays are driven through a 6821 Peripheral Interface Adapter. To detect open wiring harnesses, blown solenoid coils, or shorted circuits, the controller periodically cycles each driver line and reads back the electrical logic level. Configured in factory calibrations to fifty-eight counts, PIAMSK establishes which output driver circuits on Port A are actively evaluated for electrical continuity faults. Monitored circuits include the radiator fan relay, air conditioning clutch relay, automatic shutdown relay, canister purge solenoid, check engine light, part throttle unlock solenoid, and cruise control solenoids.
PIAMSK.overview_markdown:
`PIAMSK` defines the diagnostic output driver circuit mask for Port A of the Peripheral Interface Adapter.

In Chrysler SMEC engine controllers, high-current inductive drivers and relays are driven through a 6821 Peripheral Interface Adapter. To detect open wiring harnesses, blown solenoid coils, or shorted circuits, the controller periodically cycles each driver line and reads back the electrical logic level. Configured in factory calibrations to fifty-eight counts, `PIAMSK` establishes which output driver circuits on Port A are actively evaluated for electrical continuity faults. Monitored circuits include the radiator fan relay, air conditioning clutch relay, automatic shutdown relay, canister purge solenoid, check engine light, part throttle unlock solenoid, and cruise control solenoids.
PIAMSK.tuners_guide: When simplifying engine bays or deleting auxiliary vehicle subsystems, clearing the corresponding bit in PIAMSK disables diagnostic circuit testing for that specific output driver. For example, if the charcoal canister evaporative purge solenoid is removed, clearing the purge solenoid bit prevents the controller from flagging an open-circuit fault. Similarly, if the air conditioning compressor clutch relay or cruise control vacuum solenoids are removed, clearing their respective bits in PIAMSK suppresses diagnostic testing on those pins without affecting radiator fan or automatic shutdown relay operation.
PIAMSK.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Auxiliary Driver Deletions**:
  * Clearing specific bits in `PIAMSK` disables hardware circuit integrity tests on removed relays or solenoids.
* **Monitored Port A Circuits**:
  * Purge solenoid, A/C clutch relay, radiator fan relay, ASD relay, check engine lamp, and cruise solenoids.
* **Ghost Error Prevention**:
  * Prevents open-circuit error codes when eliminating comfort accessories or evaporative purge hardware.
* **Factory Default**:
  * Set to fifty-eight counts, actively monitoring purge, fan, A/C, and ASD circuits.
PIAMSK.operating_conditions:
* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `UPDATE_PIA1_A_PDR_DDR_REGISTER` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:4331-4375`), instruction line 4349 (`bita PIAMSK_PIA1ADDRMask`).
* **Hardware Feedback Loop**:
  * Port A pins are pulsed and read back during main loop passes.
  * Loop counter bits (`Counter_MainLoop & 0x07`) select which driver pin is verified.
* **Comparison & Branch**:
  * If `bita PIAMSK_PIA1ADDRMask` is zero (`beq L1314`), diagnostic error testing for that pin is bypassed.
  * If unmasked and the read-back level indicates a circuit fault, branches to `ThrowCriticalError` or `ThrowNonCriticalError`.

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In `UPDATE_PIA1_A_PDR_DDR_REGISTER` at lines 4343-4350, the CPU reads back the actual logic states from `PIA1_PortA_DataDirection` and exclusive-ORs them against the commanded buffer. At line 4349, `bita PIAMSK_PIA1ADDRMask` masks the resulting error bits. If clear (`beq L1314`), circuit error logging is skipped. If set, lines 4363-4374 execute `ThrowCriticalError` or `ThrowNonCriticalError` to store the failure.
technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
; --- UPDATE_PIA1_A_PDR_DDR_REGISTER (T-SMEC_v19.asm:4343-4357) ---
	eora PIA1_PortA_DataDirection
	ldx  #PIA1AManipulation_Table	    ; load index with value
	ldab Counter_MainLoop	  ; load b with memory contents
	andb #0x07	    ;  -00000111-
	abx		    ; add b to index
	anda 0x00,x	
	bita PIAMSK_PIA1ADDRMask	  ;  (data is 3a)
	beq  L1314	    ; branch if no bits are set
	cmpb #0x03	    ;  -00000011-
	bne  L1312	    ; branch if not equal (not zero)
	tst  CONFIG_ConfigurationFlags	  ;  (data is 02)
	bpl  L1311	    ; branch if plus (hi bit 0)
	brclr *PIA1_A_Buffer, #pia1abuf_FanRelay, L1312    ; branch if bit(s) clear
	bra  L1314	    ; branch

PIAMSK.calibration_notes:
* **Bit Allocations**: Bit 6: Purge Solenoid, Bit 5: Part Throttle Unlock, Bit 4: A/C Clutch Relay, Bit 3: Fan Relay, Bit 1: ASD Relay, Bit 0: Cruise Solenoids.
* **Port Pair**: Companion to `PIBMSK` which manages Port B driver circuits.
* **Safety Interlocks**: Includes countdown timers from key-on to allow inductive coil flyback voltages to settle before testing.

PIBMSK.overview: PIBMSK defines the diagnostic output driver circuit mask for Port B of the Peripheral Interface Adapter. Port B controls dedicated powertrain inductive solenoids and warning indicators, including the exhaust gas recirculation solenoid, turbocharger wastegate control solenoid, barometric read solenoid, and emissions maintenance reminder lamp. Configured in factory calibrations to two hundred twenty-four counts, PIBMSK dictates which of these output circuits are actively tested for open coils, wiring breaks, or driver circuit failures during vehicle operation.
PIBMSK.overview_markdown:
`PIBMSK` defines the diagnostic output driver circuit mask for Port B of the Peripheral Interface Adapter.

Port B controls dedicated powertrain inductive solenoids and warning indicators, including the exhaust gas recirculation solenoid, turbocharger wastegate control solenoid, barometric read solenoid, and emissions maintenance reminder lamp. Configured in factory calibrations to two hundred twenty-four counts, `PIBMSK` dictates which of these output circuits are actively tested for open coils, wiring breaks, or driver circuit failures during vehicle operation.
PIBMSK.tuners_guide: PIBMSK is frequently adjusted when installing aftermarket boost control equipment or removing factory emissions hardware. When replacing the factory computer-controlled wastegate solenoid with a manual boost controller, clearing the wastegate solenoid switch in PIBMSK disables electrical continuity testing on that pin, preventing the computer from logging fault code thirty-six. Similarly, clearing the exhaust gas recirculation solenoid bit stops circuit diagnostics when an EGR block-off plate is installed, keeping the diagnostic log clean.
PIBMSK.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Wastegate Solenoid Circuit Testing**:
  * Clearing the wastegate solenoid bit stops electrical driver line testing on Port B, preventing fault code 36 when the solenoid is removed.
* **EGR Solenoid Circuit Testing**:
  * Clearing the EGR solenoid bit disables circuit feedback checks when deleting emissions components.
* **Barometric Solenoid Testing**:
  * Allows disabling diagnostics on the baro read solenoid if non-stock atmospheric sensing is implemented.
* **Factory Default**:
  * Set to two hundred twenty-four counts, actively monitoring EGR, wastegate, and baro read circuits.
PIBMSK.operating_conditions:
* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `UPDATE_PIA1_A_PDR_DDR_REGISTER` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:4331-4420`), instruction line 4407 (`bita PIBMSK_PIA1BDDRMask`).
* **Driver Verification**:
  * Executes sequentially following Port A verification.
  * Uses `Counter_MainLoop & 0x07` to select the active Port B output pin.
* **Branch Execution**:
  * If `bita PIBMSK_PIA1BDDRMask` is zero (`beq R1318`), testing on the pin is skipped.
  * If set and an open circuit is detected on the wastegate driver, calls `ThrowNonCriticalError` and sets `b46_WGSolFault`.

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In `UPDATE_PIA1_A_PDR_DDR_REGISTER` at lines 4404-4408, accumulator A holds the exclusive-OR feedback from `PIA1_PortB_DataDirection`. At line 4407, `bita PIBMSK_PIA1BDDRMask` masks the driver circuit test. If zero (`beq R1318`), testing is bypassed. If set, lines 4411-4418 verify pin state; if the wastegate solenoid is faulted, `ThrowNonCriticalError` is called with error code 0x0D (fault 36) and `b46_WGSolFault` is set in `b46_IPL2`.
technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
; --- UPDATE_PIA1_A_PDR_DDR_REGISTER (T-SMEC_v19.asm:4404-4419) ---
	eora PIA1_PortB_DataDirection
	cli		    ; enable interrupts
	anda 0x00,x	
	bita PIBMSK_PIA1BDDRMask	  ;  (data is e0)
	beq  R1318	    ; branch if equal (zero)
	ldaa CountdownTimerFromKeyOn	; load a with memory contents
	bne  R1318	    ; branch if not equal (not zero)
	ldaa 0x10,x	    ; load a with memory at index + value
	cmpa #0x0d	    ; compare a with value -00001101-
	bne  L1316	    ; branch if not equal (not zero)
	brset *b46_IPL2, #b46_WGSolFault, R1318	; branch if bit(s) set
	ldab #0xa0	    ; load b with value -10100000-
	bsr  ThrowNonCriticalError    ; call subroutine
	bcc  R1318	    ; branch if greater or equal
	bset *b46_IPL2, #b46_WGSolFault	; set bits
	rts		    ; return from subroutine

PIBMSK.calibration_notes:
* **Bit Allocations**: Bit 7: EGR Solenoid, Bit 6: Wastegate Solenoid, Bit 5: Baro Read Solenoid, Bit 4: Emission Light.
* **Wastegate Fault Latching**: Sets `b46_WGSolFault` when an unmasked wastegate solenoid driver fault occurs.
* **Companion Mask**: Works directly with `PIAMSK`.

PNDLT.overview: PNDLT defines the engine speed error deadband threshold required before the controller triggers the automatic transmission Park/Neutral to Drive kick opening table. When the driver shifts an automatic transmission from Park or Neutral into Drive or Reverse, the transmission hydraulic clutches engage and the torque converter impeller suddenly loads the crankshaft. To prevent the resulting mechanical drag from causing a severe engine stumble or stall, the ECU monitors the RPM drop. If the difference between actual engine speed and target idle speed exceeds PNDLT, the controller advances its memory pointer to index the PNDRK opening step table. In factory calibrations, PNDLT is configured to 400 counts, representing an RPM delta trigger threshold of approximately 200 RPM.
PNDLT.overview_markdown:
`PNDLT` defines the engine speed error deadband threshold required before the controller triggers the automatic transmission Park/Neutral to Drive kick opening table.

When the driver shifts an automatic transmission from Park or Neutral into Drive or Reverse, the transmission hydraulic clutches engage and the torque converter impeller suddenly loads the crankshaft. To prevent the resulting mechanical drag from causing a severe engine stumble or stall, the ECU monitors the RPM drop.

If the difference between actual engine speed and target idle speed exceeds `PNDLT`, the controller advances its memory pointer to index the `PNDRK` opening step table.

In factory calibrations, `PNDLT` is configured to 400 counts, representing an RPM delta trigger threshold of approximately 200 RPM.
PNDLT.tuners_guide: PNDLT controls how quickly the ECU intervenes when shifting into gear. If shifting into Drive causes the engine RPM to sag deeply or die before the idle controller reacts, lowering PNDLT to 100 to 150 RPM (200 to 300 counts) makes the ECU trigger the PNDRK step kick at a smaller initial RPM drop, catching the engine earlier. However, if PNDLT is set too low (below 50 RPM), minor engine speed fluctuations in neutral can accidentally trigger the in-gear kick, causing unwanted idle flaring. For loose, high-stall aftermarket torque converters that produce very little idle drag, PNDLT can be raised to prevent premature step kicks.
PNDLT.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Earlier In-Gear Catch**:
  * Lower `PNDLT` from 200 RPM down to 100 to 140 RPM to trigger the `PNDRK` kick sooner if the engine dips heavily when shifted into Drive.
* **High-Stall Torque Converters**:
  * High-stall converters generate less initial drag; `PNDLT` can be elevated to prevent unnecessary step kicks on gear selection.
* **Threshold Minimum**:
  * Do not lower `PNDLT` below 50 RPM to avoid false triggering from natural idle lope.
PNDLT.operating_conditions:
* **Enclosing Routine**: `HandleAcCutout` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:2170-2365`) within `CalculateTargetIdleSpeedAndAisPosition_MM`.
* **Gating Conditions**:
  * Automatic transmission gear change active: `b0c_ATXChngGear` set in `BitFlags_AIS` at line 2344.
  * Shifting into gear: `b0c_ATXInGear` clear at line 2345 (branches to `L1126`).
  * Loads index X with `#PNDLTN_DeltaRpmChangeToUse_DRPNK_or_PNDRK` at line 2351.
  * Calculates RPM drop: `ldd EngineRpm_HB; subd TargetIdleSpeed_HB`.
  * Compares delta against `PNDLT` at line 2355: `subd 0x00,x`. If delta exceeds `PNDLT` (carry clear), advances via `inx; inx` to look up `PNDRK`.

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In `CalculateTargetIdleSpeedAndAisPosition_MM`, line 2345 branches to label `L1126` when shifting into gear. Line 2351 loads index X with `#PNDLTN_DeltaRpmChangeToUse_DRPNK_or_PNDRK`. Lines 2352-2353 compute `ldd EngineRpm_HB; subd TargetIdleSpeed_HB`. At line 2355, the CPU subtracts the 16-bit word pointed to by X: `subd 0x00,x`. If carry is set (`bcs L1130`), the RPM error is below `PNDLT` and the kick is skipped. If carry is clear, lines 2358-2359 execute `inx; inx` to advance index X past the 2-byte `PNDLT` word to point directly to `PNDRK`.
technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
; --- HandleAcCutout (T-SMEC_v19.asm:2350-2362) ---

L1126:	ldx  #PNDLTN_DeltaRpmChangeToUse_DRPNK_or_PNDRK    ; load index with value
	ldd  EngineRpm_HB    ; load d (a&b) with memory contents
	subd TargetIdleSpeed_HB	; d = d - memory contents
L1127:	bcs  L1130	    ; branch if lower
	subd 0x00,x	
	bcs  L1130	    ; branch if lower
	ldaa CoolantTemp    ; load a with memory contents
	inx		    ; increment index (x=x+1)
	inx		    ; increment index (x=x+1)
	jsr  Lookup4ByteTable	 ; call subroutine
	bmi  L1128	    ; branch if minus(hi bit 1)
	jsr  MultiplyTempvar1ByA    ; call subroutine

PNDLT.calibration_notes:
* **Label Spelling**: Identified as `PNDLT` in template headers and `PNDLTN_DeltaRpmChangeToUse_DRPNK_or_PNDRK` in ROM labels.
* **Pointer Architecture**: Sits immediately prior to `PNDRK` in ROM memory; the CPU steps directly from `PNDLT` into `PNDRK` via `inx; inx`.
* **Word-Length Constant**: Type 4 (16-bit word), factory value 0x0190 (400 counts = ~200 RPM).

PNDLTP.overview: PNDLTP defines the engine speed error threshold required before the controller triggers the automatic transmission Drive to Park/Neutral step reduction table. When the driver shifts an automatic transmission out of Drive or Reverse into Park or Neutral, the hydraulic load of the torque converter is suddenly released from the crankshaft. If the idle air stepper motor remained in its loaded in-gear position, the sudden uncoupling of transmission drag would cause the engine to flare upward loudly into a high-RPM surge. To prevent this flare, the ECU detects the RPM change upon shifting out of gear. If the difference between target idle speed and actual engine speed exceeds PNDLTP, the controller advances its memory pointer to index the DRPNK closing step table. In factory calibrations, PNDLTP is set to 160 counts, representing an RPM delta trigger threshold of approximately 80 RPM.
PNDLTP.overview_markdown:
`PNDLTP` defines the engine speed error threshold required before the controller triggers the automatic transmission Drive to Park/Neutral step reduction table.

When the driver shifts an automatic transmission out of Drive or Reverse into Park or Neutral, the hydraulic load of the torque converter is suddenly released from the crankshaft. If the idle air stepper motor remained in its loaded in-gear position, the sudden uncoupling of transmission drag would cause the engine to flare upward loudly into a high-RPM surge.

To prevent this flare, the ECU detects the RPM change upon shifting out of gear.

If the difference between target idle speed and actual engine speed exceeds `PNDLTP`, the controller advances its memory pointer to index the `DRPNK` closing step table.

In factory calibrations, `PNDLTP` is set to 160 counts, representing an RPM delta trigger threshold of approximately 80 RPM.
PNDLTP.tuners_guide: PNDLTP controls how sensitive the ECU is to shifting out of gear. If shifting from Drive to Park or Neutral results in an annoying engine flare where RPM shoots up past 1400 RPM before settling, lowering PNDLTP to 50 to 60 RPM (100 to 120 counts) triggers the DRPNK step reduction sooner, snuffing out the flare before it starts. If set too low (below 30 RPM), normal in-gear idle speed dithering can prematurely trigger the step reduction, causing the engine to sag while still in gear. Retain factory setting (80 RPM) for stock torque converters.
PNDLTP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Eliminating Neutral Shift Flare**:
  * Lower `PNDLTP` to 50 to 65 RPM if the engine flares upward loudly when shifting out of gear into Park or Neutral.
* **Threshold Minimum**:
  * Do not set `PNDLTP` below 30 RPM to avoid false triggering from natural idle speed oscillations.
* **Complementary Trigger**:
  * Direct counterpart to `PNDLT`, governing the opposite shift transition.
PNDLTP.operating_conditions:
* **Enclosing Routine**: `HandleAcCutout` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:2170-2365`) within `CalculateTargetIdleSpeedAndAisPosition_MM`.
* **Gating Conditions**:
  * Automatic transmission gear change active: `b0c_ATXChngGear` set in `BitFlags_AIS` at line 2344.
  * Shifting out of gear: `b0c_ATXInGear` set at line 2345.
  * Loads index X with `#PNDLTP_DeltaRpmChangeToUse_DRPNK_or_PNDRK` at line 2346.
  * Calculates RPM delta: `ldd TargetIdleSpeed_HB; subd EngineRpm_HB`.
  * Compares delta against `PNDLTP` at line 2355: `subd 0x00,x`. If delta exceeds `PNDLTP` (carry clear), advances via `inx; inx` to look up `DRPNK`.

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In `CalculateTargetIdleSpeedAndAisPosition_MM`, line 2345 checks `b0c_ATXInGear`. When shifting out of gear (in-gear bit set), line 2346 loads index X with `#PNDLTP_DeltaRpmChangeToUse_DRPNK_or_PNDRK`. Lines 2347-2348 compute `ldd TargetIdleSpeed_HB; subd EngineRpm_HB`. Line 2349 branches to `L1127`. Line 2355 executes `subd 0x00,x`. If carry is set (`bcs L1130`), the error is below `PNDLTP` and execution aborts. If carry is clear, lines 2358-2359 execute `inx; inx` to advance index X to point to `DRPNK`.
