RPMDEF.overview: RPMDEF defines the default baseline engine speed target utilized by the idle control logic during engine cranking and initial stall recovery. When the starter motor is turning the crankshaft, actual engine speed is typically only 150 to 250 RPM, which is well below normal operating idle speed. If the closed-loop idle control routines were allowed to calculate an error delta against true engine cranking speed, the proportional and integral feedback loops would saturate, commanding maximum opening steps and causing severe over-fueling or high-RPM flare upon catching. To prevent this control loop windup, whenever engine speed is below the threshold set in RPMTHS, the SMEC substitutes RPMDEF as a synthetic engine speed target. In factory calibrations, RPMDEF is set to 160 counts, representing an equivalent engine speed target of approximately 1280 RPM.
RPMDEF.overview_markdown:
`RPMDEF` defines the default baseline engine speed target utilized by the idle control logic during engine cranking and initial stall recovery.

When the starter motor is turning the crankshaft, actual engine speed is typically only 150 to 250 RPM, which is well below normal operating idle speed. If the closed-loop idle control routines were allowed to calculate an error delta against true engine cranking speed, the proportional and integral feedback loops would saturate, commanding maximum opening steps and causing severe over-fueling or high-RPM flare upon catching.

To prevent this control loop windup, whenever engine speed is below the threshold set in `RPMTHS`, the SMEC substitutes `RPMDEF` as a synthetic engine speed target.

In factory calibrations, `RPMDEF` is set to 160 counts, representing an equivalent engine speed target of approximately 1280 RPM.
RPMDEF.tuners_guide: RPMDEF should generally remain at its factory setting of 1280 RPM for the majority of street and performance builds. Raising RPMDEF primes the idle controller with a higher synthetic speed target during the transition from starter cranking to engine firing, which can help aggressive camshaft profiles catch and clear out loaded intake tracts. However, raising RPMDEF too high will cause excessive stepper motor opening during cranking, leading to an aggressive flare that overshoots target idle upon starting. Lowering RPMDEF reduces the initial airflow target; if lowered too far, the engine may struggle to sustain run mode after the starter disengages, resulting in cold cranking die-out.
RPMDEF.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Factory Baseline**:
  * Keep `RPMDEF` at 160 counts (1280 RPM) for stock and mild street calibrations.
* **Aggressive Camshaft Catch**:
  * For race camshafts with significant overlap, raising `RPMDEF` to 1350 to 1450 RPM can help the engine bridge the transition from cranking to steady idle.
* **Overshoot & Flare Warning**:
  * Setting `RPMDEF` higher than 1500 RPM produces excessive throttle flare upon initial firing.

RPMDLT.overview: RPMDLT defines the engine speed tolerance adder above target idle speed that permits entry into rolling idle mode on manual transmission vehicles. While coasting in neutral below the speed threshold set in AISMPH, the engine controller must decide whether engine speed is close enough to target idle to engage closed-loop rolling idle regulation. If actual engine speed is significantly higher than target idle (for instance, if the driver just downshifted or revved the engine), entering rolling idle mode prematurely would cause the controller to actively fight the descending revs. RPMDLT is added to target idle speed to form an upper RPM boundary. Only when actual engine speed is below this combined threshold is rolling idle mode activated. In factory calibrations, RPMDLT is set to 7 counts, corresponding to an RPM tolerance of approximately 56 RPM.
RPMDLT.overview_markdown:
`RPMDLT` defines the engine speed tolerance adder above target idle speed that permits entry into rolling idle mode on manual transmission vehicles.

While coasting in neutral below the speed threshold set in `AISMPH`, the engine controller must decide whether engine speed is close enough to target idle to engage closed-loop rolling idle regulation. If actual engine speed is significantly higher than target idle (for instance, if the driver just downshifted or revved the engine), entering rolling idle mode prematurely would cause the controller to actively fight the descending revs.

`RPMDLT` is added to target idle speed to form an upper RPM boundary. Only when actual engine speed is below this combined threshold is rolling idle mode activated.

In factory calibrations, `RPMDLT` is set to 7 counts, corresponding to an RPM tolerance of approximately 56 RPM.
RPMDLT.tuners_guide: RPMDLT sets the catch window for rolling idle engagement. If you have enabled rolling idle via AISMPH but find that rolling idle takes too long to engage when coasting down toward a stop, increasing RPMDLT from 56 RPM up to 100 to 150 RPM (12 to 18 counts) allows the controller to engage rolling idle mode while engine speed is still descending. This provides a smoother hand-off into closed-loop idle speed regulation. Do not set RPMDLT above 250 RPM, as the controller will attempt to engage idle speed control while the engine is still at normal driving RPM.

  * Increase `RPMDLT` to 100 to 150 RPM to allow rolling idle mode to engage earlier as engine speed drops toward idle while coasting.
* **Factory Tolerance**:
  * Factory setting of 56 RPM (7 counts) requires engine speed to settle very close to target idle before rolling idle locks in.
* **Upper Boundary Warning**:
  * Keep `RPMDLT` below 250 RPM to avoid false idle mode triggering during high-RPM coast-down.

RPMLIM.overview: RPMLIM establishes the upper engine speed limit for closed-loop oxygen sensor feedback and adaptive fuel memory updates. At high engine speeds, rapid valve timing and high exhaust gas velocity reduce the precision of narrowband oxygen sensor feedback, while engine load demands favor rich, open-loop power enrichment. In factory calibrations, RPMLIM is configured to 86 counts in high-byte RPM scaling (where each count represents 32 RPM), setting the threshold at 2752 RPM. Above this speed, the engine controller locks out closed loop and operates in open loop.
RPMLIM.overview_markdown:
`RPMLIM` establishes the upper engine speed limit for closed-loop oxygen sensor feedback and adaptive fuel memory updates.

At high engine speeds, rapid valve timing and high exhaust gas velocity reduce the precision of narrowband oxygen sensor feedback, while engine load demands favor rich, open-loop power enrichment.

In factory calibrations, `RPMLIM` is configured to 86 counts in high-byte RPM scaling (where each count represents 32 RPM), setting the threshold at 2752 RPM. Above this speed, the engine controller locks out closed loop and operates in open loop.
RPMLIM.tuners_guide: Raising RPMLIM extends closed-loop stoichiometric fuel control and adaptive trim learning to higher cruising engine speeds. For manual transmission vehicles or vehicles with aggressive differential gearing that cruise at 3000 to 3400 RPM on the highway, raising RPMLIM to 110 or 120 counts (3520 to 3840 RPM) allows the controller to maintain closed-loop fuel economy during highway travel. Lowering RPMLIM forces the engine into open-loop fueling earlier in the rev range, which is desirable on road-race builds where sustained mid-range operation requires rich air-fuel ratios for exhaust valve protection.
RPMLIM.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Highway Cruising Extension**:
  * Raising `RPMLIM` to 100-115 counts (3200-3680 RPM) maintains closed-loop fuel economy on vehicles with short final drive gearing.
* **Race Applications**:
  * Lowering `RPMLIM` to 2200-2400 RPM forces early open loop, protecting exhaust valves with rich mixtures during aggressive driving.
* **RPM Scaling**:
  * High-byte engine speed scaling (1 count = 32 RPM; 86 counts = 2752 RPM).

RPMLMT.overview: RPMLMT defines an RPM-indexed upper limit ceiling on warm part-throttle manifold pressure spark advance. Under light throttle and deep manifold vacuum at low engine speeds, the theoretical mathematical sum of mechanical advance and part-throttle vacuum advance could command excessive total timing that causes low-RPM bucking, surging, or misfires. RPMLMT caps the maximum positive advance that HOTMAP can produce as a function of engine speed, ensuring that part-throttle timing ramps up in a controlled, smooth progression as engine speed rises.
RPMLMT.overview_markdown:
`RPMLMT` defines an RPM-indexed upper limit ceiling on warm part-throttle manifold pressure spark advance.

Under light throttle and deep manifold vacuum at low engine speeds, the theoretical mathematical sum of mechanical advance and part-throttle vacuum advance could command excessive total timing that causes low-RPM bucking, surging, or misfires. `RPMLMT` caps the maximum positive advance that `HOTMAP` can produce as a function of engine speed, ensuring that part-throttle timing ramps up in a controlled, smooth progression as engine speed rises.
RPMLMT.tuners_guide: Raising values in RPMLMT allows more positive part-throttle MAP advance at lower engine speeds, providing crisper light-throttle response on responsive, lightweight vehicles. However, raising it excessively at low engine speeds can cause light-throttle surging or bucking. Lowering values in RPMLMT restricts part-throttle timing, smoothing out low-speed drivability and calming nervous throttle response in heavy traffic or on vehicles equipped with lightened flywheels.
RPMLMT.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Low-RPM Drivability Smoothing**:
  * Lowering `RPMLMT` below 2500 RPM prevents excessive vacuum advance, eliminating light-throttle bucking or jerking.
* **Throttle Response Improvement**:
  * Raising `RPMLMT` allows the engine to pull more vacuum advance during off-idle transitions, sharpening low-end engine response.
* **Capping Part-Throttle Advance**:
  * Functions specifically as an upper boundary on `HOTMAP`, ensuring advance increases smoothly with RPM.

RPMMAP.overview: RPMMAP defines the manifold pressure threshold curve across engine speed that separates the increasing part-throttle enrichment zone from the decreasing part-throttle enrichment zone. During moderate to heavy acceleration before wide-open throttle is reached, the engine controller requires open-loop fuel enrichment to prevent lean misfires and assist turbocharger spool-up. The controller looks up the switchpoint from RPMMAP based on current engine speed and compares it to manifold absolute pressure. When manifold pressure exceeds the curve, the controller increments the open-loop enrichment multiplier. When manifold pressure falls below the curve, the controller decrements the enrichment multiplier back toward baseline. The factory curve transitions from positive boost of approximately 3.1 psi at 2900 RPM down to 9.2 psi of vacuum at 5200 RPM.
RPMMAP.overview_markdown:
`RPMMAP` defines the manifold pressure threshold curve across engine speed that separates the increasing part-throttle enrichment zone from the decreasing part-throttle enrichment zone.

During moderate to heavy acceleration before wide-open throttle is reached, the engine controller requires open-loop fuel enrichment to prevent lean misfires and assist turbocharger spool-up. The controller looks up the switchpoint from `RPMMAP` based on current engine speed and compares it to manifold absolute pressure.

When manifold pressure exceeds the curve, the controller increments the open-loop enrichment multiplier. When manifold pressure falls below the curve, the controller decrements the enrichment multiplier back toward baseline. The factory curve transitions from positive boost of approximately 3.1 psi at 2900 RPM down to 9.2 psi of vacuum at 5200 RPM.
RPMMAP.tuners_guide: Adjust RPMMAP to control the engine load threshold where aggressive part-throttle boost enrichment begins. Lowering table pressure values causes the controller to trigger part-throttle enrichment earlier in the manifold pressure sweep, eliminating lean flat spots and hesitation during moderate pedal tip-in. Raising table pressure values delays enrichment until higher manifold boost levels are attained, improving fuel economy during light-load highway cruising. When tuning vehicles converted to 3-bar MAP sensors, rescale table pressure values so that the intended boost and vacuum trigger boundaries correspond accurately to the new sensor voltage scaling.
RPMMAP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Enrichment Onset Threshold**: Lowering table pressure values causes the controller to trigger part-throttle enrichment earlier in the manifold pressure sweep, eliminating lean flat spots and hesitation during moderate pedal tip-in.
* **Highway Cruise Economy**: Raising table pressure values delays enrichment until higher manifold boost levels are attained, improving fuel economy during light-load highway cruising.
* **3-Bar MAP Recalibration**: When tuning vehicles converted to 3-bar MAP sensors, rescale table pressure values so that the intended boost and vacuum trigger boundaries correspond accurately to the new sensor voltage scaling.
* **Camshaft and Drivability Matching**: Engines with high-flow cylinder heads or free-flowing exhaust systems spool turbos faster, often benefiting from a flatter threshold curve that enriches fueling as soon as positive manifold pressure builds.

RPMPOS.overview: RPMPOS is a 2D calibration curve that establishes a minimum automatic idle speed stepper motor opening based purely on engine RPM. Even if the throttle is only cracked open slightly, high engine RPM creates massive engine vacuum demand when the throttle plate suddenly snaps shut. If the idle air stepper motor were sitting fully closed during high-RPM deceleration, the sudden throttle closure would create an extreme intake manifold vacuum spike, sucking oil past valve guide seals and causing severe engine braking or sudden stalling. RPMPOS monitors engine speed and enforces a progressively higher minimum stepper opening floor as engine RPM rises. In factory calibrations, RPMPOS commands 0 steps below 1000 RPM, transitioning to 3 steps around 1500 RPM, and 6 steps above 2250 RPM.
RPMPOS.overview_markdown:
`RPMPOS` is a 2D calibration curve that establishes a minimum automatic idle speed stepper motor opening based purely on engine RPM.

Even if the throttle is only cracked open slightly, high engine RPM creates massive engine vacuum demand when the throttle plate suddenly snaps shut. If the idle air stepper motor were sitting fully closed during high-RPM deceleration, the sudden throttle closure would create an extreme intake manifold vacuum spike, sucking oil past valve guide seals and causing severe engine braking or sudden stalling.

`RPMPOS` monitors engine speed and enforces a progressively higher minimum stepper opening floor as engine RPM rises.

In factory calibrations, `RPMPOS` commands 0 steps below 1000 RPM, transitioning to 3 steps around 1500 RPM, and 6 steps above 2250 RPM.
RPMPOS.tuners_guide: RPMPOS provides an electronic dashpot cushion that prevents deceleration stalling from high engine speeds. If your engine dips below idle or stalls when you rev the engine in neutral and let off the throttle, or when you disengage the clutch at high RPM, increasing the step values in RPMPOS above 2000 RPM will keep the idle valve propped open to catch the descending engine speed. On cars with lightweight flywheels, increasing RPMPOS values by 3 to 5 steps provides critical decel air cushion. However, do not set RPMPOS values excessively high, as this will reduce engine braking and cause the car to feel like the throttle is sticking open when decelerating in gear.
RPMPOS.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **High-RPM Decel Stall Catch**:
  * Increase `RPMPOS` step values above 2000 RPM if the engine stalls when abruptly releasing the throttle from high RPM.
* **Lightweight Flywheels**:
  * Add 3 to 6 steps to `RPMPOS` to catch lightweight rotating assemblies that drop revs too quickly on clutch disengagement.
* **Excessive Hang Warning**:
  * Setting `RPMPOS` too high causes the engine to coast forward with unwanted forward push and diminished engine braking.

RPMPOS.raw_text: OVERVIEW: RPMPOS is a 2D calibration curve that establishes a minimum automatic idle speed stepper motor opening based purely on engine RPM. Even if the throttle is only cracked open slightly, high engine RPM creates massive engine vacuum demand when the throttle plate suddenly snaps shut. If the idle air stepper motor were sitting fully closed during high-RPM deceleration, the sudden throttle closure would create an extreme intake manifold vacuum spike, sucking oil past valve guide seals and causing severe engine braking or sudden stalling. RPMPOS monitors engine speed and enforces a progressively higher minimum stepper opening floor as engine RPM rises. In factory calibrations, RPMPOS commands 0 steps below 1000 RPM, transitioning to 3 steps around 1500 RPM, and 6 steps above 2250 RPM. | TUNER'S GUIDE: RPMPOS provides an electronic dashpot cushion that prevents deceleration stalling from high engine speeds. If your engine dips below idle or stalls when you rev the engine in neutral and let off the throttle, or when you disengage the clutch at high RPM, increasing the step values in RPMPOS above 2000 RPM will keep the idle valve propped open to catch the descending engine speed. On cars with lightweight flywheels, increasing RPMPOS values by 3 to 5 steps provides critical decel air cushion. However, do not set RPMPOS values excessively high, as this will reduce engine braking and cause the car to feel like the throttle is sticking open when decelerating in gear.

RPMTHR.overview: RPMTHR defines the minimum engine speed boundary required to permit upward adaptive learning of the closed-throttle baseline voltage. When an engine decelerates, the vehicle must be traveling at sufficient speed with the engine spinning above idle to ensure high manifold vacuum and verify that the throttle plate is completely closed against its mechanical stop. In factory calibrations, RPMTHR is configured to forty-eight counts, which corresponds to approximately fifteen hundred RPM. As long as engine speed remains above fifteen hundred RPM while braking under high vacuum, the controller validates closed-throttle conditions and increments the learned minimum throttle voltage.
RPMTHR.overview_markdown:
`RPMTHR` defines the minimum engine speed boundary required to permit upward adaptive learning of the closed-throttle baseline voltage.

When an engine decelerates, the vehicle must be traveling at sufficient speed with the engine spinning above idle to ensure high manifold vacuum and verify that the throttle plate is completely closed against its mechanical stop. In factory calibrations, `RPMTHR` is configured to forty-eight counts, which corresponds to approximately fifteen hundred RPM. As long as engine speed remains above fifteen hundred RPM while braking under high vacuum, the controller validates closed-throttle conditions and increments the learned minimum throttle voltage.
RPMTHR.tuners_guide: Tuners generally leave RPMTHR at its factory setting of fifteen hundred RPM. If building a dedicated competition engine with a high target idle speed (such as twelve hundred to fourteen hundred RPM), RPMTHR should be increased to eighteen hundred or two thousand RPM so that adaptive learning occurs well above the high idle speed window. Setting RPMTHR too low could allow the computer to relearn closed throttle while the engine is lugging or returning to idle, potentially corrupting the learned idle voltage baseline.
RPMTHR.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Minimum Engine Speed for Learning**:
  * Ensures deceleration learning occurs strictly while coasting down in gear above idle speed.
* **High Idle Applications**:
  * If idle speed target is elevated above 1100 RPM for wild camshafts, raise `RPMTHR` proportionally (e.g., 1800 to 2000 RPM).
* **Prevents Low-Speed False Learning**:
  * Prevents erratic minimum throttle updates when the engine is lugging or recovering from an idle dip.
* **Factory Default**:
  * Set to forty-eight counts (~1500 RPM) in stock calibrations.

* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `CheckThrottle_VehicleSpeedStillAboveDecelIdle` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:7885-7914`), instruction line 7896 (`cmpa RPMTHR_...`).

  * If engine speed is lower (`bcs L1656`), upward learning is bypassed.

RPMTHS.overview: RPMTHS defines the engine speed threshold separating starter motor cranking or engine stall states from active engine running idle control. While the engine is being cranked by the starter or if the engine stalls and RPM drops precipitously, normal closed-loop idle speed regulation must be suspended to prevent erratic stepper motor oscillations. Whenever actual engine speed is below RPMTHS, the engine controller bypasses normal closed-loop idle routines and forces the synthetic target speed defined by RPMDEF. In factory calibrations, RPMTHS is set to 25 counts, representing an engine speed threshold of 200 RPM. Once crankshaft rotation exceeds 200 RPM, the controller recognizes that combustion has initiated and begins transitioning toward normal closed-loop idle air control.
RPMTHS.overview_markdown:
`RPMTHS` defines the engine speed threshold separating starter motor cranking or engine stall states from active engine running idle control.

While the engine is being cranked by the starter or if the engine stalls and RPM drops precipitously, normal closed-loop idle speed regulation must be suspended to prevent erratic stepper motor oscillations. Whenever actual engine speed is below `RPMTHS`, the engine controller bypasses normal closed-loop idle routines and forces the synthetic target speed defined by `RPMDEF`.

In factory calibrations, `RPMTHS` is set to 25 counts, representing an engine speed threshold of 200 RPM.

Once crankshaft rotation exceeds 200 RPM, the controller recognizes that combustion has initiated and begins transitioning toward normal closed-loop idle air control.
RPMTHS.tuners_guide: RPMTHS should remain at its factory setting of 200 RPM under almost all circumstances. This threshold ensures a clean boundary between starter-driven rotation (typically 120 to 180 RPM) and genuine autonomous engine operation. If RPMTHS is set too low (for example, below 120 RPM), normal idle feedback can engage prematurely while the starter motor is still engaged, causing the stepper motor to hunt or surge before the engine is even running. Conversely, raising RPMTHS too high (above 400 RPM) forces the engine to linger in cranking mode even after it has caught, causing delayed throttle response and an extended startup flare.
RPMTHS.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Cranking vs Running Boundary**:
  * Keep `RPMTHS` at 200 RPM (25 counts) to maintain an unambiguous separation between starter cranking and autonomous engine idle.
* **Low Setting Danger**:
  * Lowering `RPMTHS` below starter cranking speed causes premature engagement of closed-loop idle feedback, inducing stepper motor hunting during cranking.
* **High Setting Delay**:
  * Setting `RPMTHS` too high traps the controller in startup mode after firing, delaying normal closed-loop idle regulation.

RTRDRT.overview: RTRDRT defines the step-size of knock retard applied to a knocking cylinder when knock is detected out of boost (under vacuum or light load below KNKOFS). When combustion knock occurs under light load or partial-throttle cruising, cylinder charge density is relatively low. Under these conditions, pulling a substantial, decisive step of ignition timing quickly extinguishes the knock without significantly disturbing vehicle momentum or causing driveline shudder. In factory calibrations, RTRDRT is set to 6 counts, corresponding to 3.0 degrees of retard applied to the active cylinder's individual retard variable upon knock detection.
RTRDRT.overview_markdown:
`RTRDRT` defines the step-size of knock retard applied to a knocking cylinder when knock is detected out of boost (under vacuum or light load below `KNKOFS`).

When combustion knock occurs under light load or partial-throttle cruising, cylinder charge density is relatively low. Under these conditions, pulling a substantial, decisive step of ignition timing quickly extinguishes the knock without significantly disturbing vehicle momentum or causing driveline shudder. In factory calibrations, `RTRDRT` is set to 6 counts, corresponding to 3.0 degrees of retard applied to the active cylinder's individual retard variable upon knock detection.
RTRDRT.tuners_guide: Raising RTRDRT pulls a larger chunk of timing (e.g., 4.0 or 5.0 degrees) on the very first knock event out of boost, providing rapid suppression of transient light-load pinging. However, pulling excessively large timing steps under light load can cause a momentary jerk or stumble in driving feel. Lowering RTRDRT applies smaller retard increments (e.g., 1.5 or 2.0 degrees), which produces smoother recovery from light-load knock, but if fuel octane is poor, multiple consecutive knock cycles may occur before sufficient timing is removed to quell the knock.
RTRDRT.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Decisive Knock Suppression**:
  * Factory setting of 3.0 degrees (6 counts) pulls enough timing on the first detection to snuff out light-load knock immediately.
* **Drivability vs. Response**:
  * Raising `RTRDRT` above 4.0 degrees can cause noticeable hesitation on tip-in ping; lowering below 2.0 degrees risks repeat pinging.
* **Per-Cylinder Application**:
  * Applied strictly to the specific cylinder that knocked, preserving full timing on the other three cylinders.
RTRDRT.operating_conditions:
* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `CHECK_FOR_OVER5PSIBOOST` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:6796-6802`), called from `CALC_SPARK_RETARD_BASED_ON_KNOCK_VOLT`.
* **Condition Tested**:
  * Active when `KnockVolts` >= `KnockSensorThreshold` and `MapValue` <= `BaroPressure + KNKOFS`.
* **Addition & Clamp**:
  * `RTRDRT` is added to the active cylinder's current retard (`aba` at line 6802).
  * Sum is clamped to 0x3F (63 counts ≈ 31.5 degrees max) and compared against `MaxRetardFromMAP`.

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In `CHECK_FOR_OVER5PSIBOOST` at line 6797, `ldaa RTRDRT_KnockRetardRateNoBoost` pre-loads the non-boost retard increment into accumulator A. If `MapValue` is less than or equal to `BaroPressure + KNKOFS`, line 6798 executes `bcc SUM_ADDITIONAL_RETARD` to line 6801. At line 6802, `aba` adds accumulator A to accumulator B (the cylinder's existing retard). The sum is checked against 0x40 at line 6803; if higher, it is clamped to 0x3F before being limited by `MaxRetardFromMAP`.

; --- CHECK_FOR_OVER5PSIBOOST (T-SMEC_v19.asm:6797-6812) ---
	ldaa RTRDRT_KnockRetardRateNoBoost    ; load a with memory contents (data is 06)
	bcc  SUM_ADDITIONAL_RETARD    ; branch if greater or equal
	bset *BitFlags_55, #b55_BoostOver5psi	 ; set bits
	ldaa RTRDRT2_KnockRetardRateInBoost	  ; load a with memory contents (data is 04)
SUM_ADDITIONAL_RETARD:
	aba		    ; a=a+b
	cmpa #0x40	    ; compare a with value -01000000-
	bcs  MAX_RETARD     ; branch if lower
	ldaa #0x3f	    ; load a with value -00111111-
MAX_RETARD:
	ldab MaxRetardFromMAP	 ; load b with memory contents
	cba		
	bcs  STORE_SMALLEST_RETARD_VALUE    ; branch if lower
	tba		    ; a = b
STORE_SMALLEST_RETARD_VALUE:
	staa 0x00,x

* **Non-Boost Specific**: Used strictly when manifold pressure is below the `KNKOFS` threshold.
* **Decay Control**: Recovered gradually in the background via `INCSRT`.

RTRDRT2.overview: RTRDRT2 defines the step-size of knock retard applied to a knocking cylinder when knock is detected under boost (manifold pressure above barometric pressure plus KNKOFS). Under positive turbocharger boost, pulling massive chunks of timing abruptly (such as 4 or 5 degrees in a single cylinder firing) can induce violent torque drops, driveline shock, and severe spikes in exhaust gas temperature. To manage boost detonation smoothly while preserving engine power delivery and component integrity, RTRDRT2 uses a finer, controlled step size (factory setting 4 counts = 2.0 degrees) applied sequentially to each knocking cylinder.
RTRDRT2.overview_markdown:
`RTRDRT2` defines the step-size of knock retard applied to a knocking cylinder when knock is detected under boost (manifold pressure above barometric pressure plus `KNKOFS`).

Under positive turbocharger boost, pulling massive chunks of timing abruptly (such as 4 or 5 degrees in a single cylinder firing) can induce violent torque drops, driveline shock, and severe spikes in exhaust gas temperature. To manage boost detonation smoothly while preserving engine power delivery and component integrity, `RTRDRT2` uses a finer, controlled step size (factory setting 4 counts = 2.0 degrees) applied sequentially to each knocking cylinder.
RTRDRT2.tuners_guide: Raising RTRDRT2 increases the in-boost retard step size (e.g., to 2.5 or 3.0 degrees), which provides aggressive, rapid timing reduction under heavy boost. This is advantageous on aggressive high-boost race setups where detonation can cause rapid component fatigue if not extinguished immediately. Lowering RTRDRT2 reduces the step size to 1.0 or 1.5 degrees, delivering smoother power delivery without sudden torque dips, but requires the base timing calibration to be very close to optimal so that small retard increments are sufficient to stop knock.
RTRDRT2.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Boost Detonation Management**:
  * Factory setting of 2.0 degrees (4 counts) balances rapid knock quenching with smooth torque delivery under boost.
* **High-Boost Aggressive Protection**:
  * On high-boost setups (18+ psi), raising `RTRDRT2` to 3.0 degrees (6 counts) pulls timing faster when boost detonation occurs.
* **Smoothness vs. Speed**:
  * Lowering `RTRDRT2` to 1.0 or 1.5 degrees produces seamless transitions during minor knock, but takes longer to accumulate total retard if severe detonation occurs.

* **Addition & Clamp**:

RUNLMT.overview: RUNLMT defines the maximum allowable coolant temperature ceiling below which post-stall heat soak temperature modeling (RUNTMP) is permitted. If an engine stalls when coolant temperature is already above RUNLMT, the engine is recognized as fully warmed up, and heat soak modeling is bypassed completely. Additionally, RUNLMT serves as the upper clamp for the simulated temperature calculation, ensuring that adding RUNTMP offset never raises effective temperature above normal warm operating levels. In factory calibrations, RUNLMT is set to 160 counts, representing approximately 145 degF.
RUNLMT.overview_markdown:
`RUNLMT` defines the maximum allowable coolant temperature ceiling below which post-stall heat soak temperature modeling (`RUNTMP`) is permitted.

If an engine stalls when coolant temperature is already above `RUNLMT`, the engine is recognized as fully warmed up, and heat soak modeling is bypassed completely. Additionally, `RUNLMT` serves as the upper clamp for the simulated temperature calculation, ensuring that adding `RUNTMP` offset never raises effective temperature above normal warm operating levels.

In factory calibrations, `RUNLMT` is set to 160 counts, representing approximately 145 degF.
RUNLMT.tuners_guide: In almost all performance and street applications, RUNLMT should remain at its factory setting of 160 counts (145 degF). Raising RUNLMT extends heat soak temperature addition up to higher coolant temperatures, which may be helpful in hot desert climates where extreme under-hood heat soak produces hard warm restarts. Lowering RUNLMT disables heat soak temperature offset sooner as the engine warms up, ensuring full cold enrichment is retained if stalling occurs during early warm-up driving. Setting RUNLMT to zero disables post-stall heat soak modeling completely.
RUNLMT.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Heat Soak Upper Ceiling**:
  * Sets the maximum coolant temperature threshold where post-stall heat soak modeling is allowed to operate.
* **Clamping Function**:
  * Clamps `CoolantTemp + RUNTMP` so simulated temperature cannot exceed `RUNLMT`.
* **Factory Setting Retention**:
  * 160 counts (approx 145 degF) correctly bounds heat soak modeling to the warm-up transition phase.
* **Disabling Heat Soak Logic**:
  * Setting `RUNLMT` to zero disables heat soak addition entirely, causing the ECU to always use raw sensor temperature.

* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `AllowForHeatSoakAfterStall` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:6243-6256`), instruction lines 6245, 6251.
* **Gating Conditions**:
  * Evaluated in `AllowForHeatSoakAfterStall`.
  * Tested against `CoolantTemp` at line 6245.
* **Branching & Clamping**:
  * If `CoolantTemp >= RUNLMT`, branches to `R1530` (returns raw coolant temp).
  * If `CoolantTemp + RUNTMP > RUNLMT`, clamps effective temperature to `RUNLMT` at lines 6251-6255.

If carry is clear (`bcc R1530`), coolant temperature is at or above `RUNLMT`, so the routine returns immediately without modifying temperature. If below `RUNLMT`, `RUNTMP` is looked up and added to accumulator A. At line 6251, `ldab RUNLMT_MaxAllowableTempFor_RUNTMP` loads the clamp limit, and lines 6253-6255 clamp accumulator A to `RUNLMT` if an overflow or higher value occurs.

	cmpa RUNLMT_MaxAllowableTempFor_RUNTMP	  ; compare a with memory contents (data is a0)
	bcc  R1530	    ; branch if greater or equal
	ldaa EngineRunningTimeBeforeStall    ; load a with memory contents
	ldx  #RUNTMP_ModifierOf_ENGTMP_FromStalltime	; load index with value
	jsr  Lookup4ByteTable	 ; call subroutine
	adda CoolantTemp
	ldab RUNLMT_MaxAllowableTempFor_RUNTMP	  ; load b with memory contents (data is a0)
	bcs  L1529	    ; branch if lower
	cba		
	bcs  R1530	    ; branch if lower
L1529:	tba		    ; a = b
R1530:	rts		    ; return from subroutine

* **Temperature Conversion**: 160 counts (0xA0) corresponds to approximately 145 degF.
* **Companion Parameter**: Direct companion to `RUNTMP`.

In factory calibrations, RUNLMT is set to 160 counts, representing approximately 145 degF. | TUNER'S GUIDE: In almost all performance and street applications, RUNLMT should remain at its factory setting of 160 counts (145 degF). Raising RUNLMT extends heat soak temperature addition up to higher coolant temperatures, which may be helpful in hot desert climates where extreme under-hood heat soak produces hard warm restarts. Lowering RUNLMT disables heat soak temperature offset sooner as the engine warms up, ensuring full cold enrichment is retained if stalling occurs during early warm-up driving. Setting RUNLMT to zero disables post-stall heat soak modeling completely.

RUNTMP.overview_markdown:
`RUNTMP` defines a coolant temperature offset curve that simulates engine heat soak following an engine stall or brief key-off.

When an engine stalls while warming up, coolant circulation stops, causing the coolant temperature sensor to cool faster than the hot cylinder block, cylinder head, and intake valves. If restarted immediately, the sensor would report a lower temperature than the physical metal surfaces, causing the ECU to inject excessive cold-start enrichment that floods the engine.

`RUNTMP` adds an artificial temperature boost based on stall duration, preventing hot restart flooding.
RUNTMP.tuners_guide: Tuning RUNTMP cures hot-restart flooding, rich stumbling, and extended cranking after an unexpected engine stall. If an engine stalls during warm-up (such as popping the clutch when pulling away) and subsequently cranks sluggishly with a strong fuel smell or flooded spark plugs, increase RUNTMP values. This adds more temperature offset, convincing the controller that the engine is warmer and reducing restart enrichment. If warm restarts after an unexpected stall pop lean in the intake manifold, reduce RUNTMP values to retain more restart fuel.
RUNTMP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Preventing Post-Stall Flooding**:
  * If stalling during warm-up causes flooded plugs and difficult restarting, increase `RUNTMP` values for stall times between 5 and 30 seconds.
* **Lean Stall Recovery**:
  * If the engine pops lean when restarted immediately after a stall, lower `RUNTMP` to preserve needed restart fuel.
* **Upper Boundary Gating**:
  * Gated by `RUNLMT`; if coolant temperature is already above `RUNLMT`, `RUNTMP` lookup is bypassed completely.
* **Added Directly to Coolant Temp**:
  * The resulting offset is added directly to `CoolantTemp` before starting and cold enrichment table lookups.

  * Gated by `cmpa RUNLMT_MaxAllowableTempFor_RUNTMP`; if `CoolantTemp >= RUNLMT`, bypassed (`bcc R1530`).
* **Math & Clamping**:
  * Looked up by `EngineRunningTimeBeforeStall`, added to `CoolantTemp` (`adda CoolantTemp`), and clamped to `RUNLMT`.

If `CoolantTemp >= RUNLMT`, line 6246 branches to `R1530` to return unaltered. If lower, line 6247 loads `EngineRunningTimeBeforeStall` into accumulator A and line 6248 loads `ldx #RUNTMP_ModifierOf_ENGTMP_FromStalltime`. `Lookup4ByteTable` executes at line 6249. At line 6250, `adda CoolantTemp` adds the offset. Lines 6251-6255 clamp the summed temperature to `RUNLMT`, returning the clamped temperature in accumulator A.

	cmpa RUNLMT_MaxAllowableTempFor_RUNTMP	  ; compare a with memory contents (data is a0)
	bcc  R1530	    ; branch if greater or equal
	ldaa EngineRunningTimeBeforeStall    ; load a with memory contents
	ldx  #RUNTMP_ModifierOf_ENGTMP_FromStalltime	; load index with value
	jsr  Lookup4ByteTable	 ; call subroutine
	adda CoolantTemp
	ldab RUNLMT_MaxAllowableTempFor_RUNTMP	  ; load b with memory contents (data is a0)
	bcs  L1529	    ; branch if lower
	cba		
	bcs  R1530	    ; branch if lower
L1529:	tba		    ; a = b
R1530:	rts		    ; return from subroutine

RVLSPD.overview: RVLSPD establishes the vehicle speed threshold that determines how the engine controller handles rev limiting when the throttle position sensor signal is invalid or failing. If the throttle position sensor produces a bad signal (for instance, an open wiper trace or erratic voltage), the controller cannot ascertain throttle blade position. If the vehicle is moving at road speeds, the controller presumes the driver is cruising and permits normal engine operation up to the standard rev limiter (REVLMT6). However, if the vehicle is stationary or moving at very low speeds, the controller enforces the restrictive plausibility rev limiter (REVLMT4 and REVLMT3) to prevent accidental runaway. In factory calibrations, RVLSPD is set to 20 counts, representing 10.0 mph on a 0 to 127.5 mph scale.
RVLSPD.overview_markdown:
`RVLSPD` establishes the vehicle speed threshold that determines how the engine controller handles rev limiting when the throttle position sensor signal is invalid or failing.

If the throttle position sensor produces a bad signal (for instance, an open wiper trace or erratic voltage), the controller cannot ascertain throttle blade position. If the vehicle is moving at road speeds, the controller presumes the driver is cruising and permits normal engine operation up to the standard rev limiter (`REVLMT6`). However, if the vehicle is stationary or moving at very low speeds, the controller enforces the restrictive plausibility rev limiter (`REVLMT4` and `REVLMT3`) to prevent accidental runaway. In factory calibrations, `RVLSPD` is set to 20 counts, representing 10.0 mph on a 0 to 127.5 mph scale.
RVLSPD.tuners_guide: RVLSPD governs low-speed safety gating when a throttle position sensor fault occurs. Raising RVLSPD to 25 or 30 mph (50 to 60 counts) ensures that the vehicle cannot be driven aggressively if the throttle sensor becomes disconnected or fails on the track, forcing the driver to pit. Lowering RVLSPD to 5 mph (10 counts) allows the vehicle to transition into standard rev limit mode almost immediately upon moving. For normal street calibrations, retaining the factory 10 mph setting ensures the engine will not rev uncontrollably in neutral or park with a broken throttle sensor while still allowing the vehicle to be driven home.
RVLSPD.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Fault Gating Threshold**:
  * When `b45_TpsBadSignal` is active, speeds above `RVLSPD` allow normal engine rev limits (`REVLMT6`), while speeds below `RVLSPD` enforce safety rev limits (`REVLMT4`).
* **Raising for Paddock Safety**:
  * Increasing `RVLSPD` to 25 mph prevents high-speed driving if the throttle sensor fails during competition.
* **Preserving Factory Setting**:
  * The 10 mph factory threshold prevents stationary runaway while allowing normal road speeds.
RVLSPD.operating_conditions:
* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `MAPSENSOR_OKAY_OR_LIGHTTHROTTLE` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:5680-5686`) and `MAPSENSOR_OKAY_OR_LIGHTTHROTTLE2` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:5783-5790`).
* **Fault Condition**:
  * Evaluated when `b45_IPL1` bit `b45_TpsBadSignal` is set.
* **Speed Comparison**:
  * Low-range vehicle speed `Temp0` (0.5 mph per count) is compared against `RVLSPD` (`cmpa RVLSPD_CarSpeedForRevLimitWithTBOff`).
  * If `Temp0 >= RVLSPD` (`bcc L1484` / `bcc L1492`), branches to select `REVLMT6` (cutout) or `REVLMT5` (restore).
  * If `Temp0 < RVLSPD`, branches to `L1483` / `L1491` to check for closed-throttle high MAP.

If carry is clear (`bcc L1484`), vehicle speed is greater than or equal to 10.0 mph, selecting `REVLMT6`. If carry is set, vehicle speed is below 10.0 mph and the code branches to `L1483`, where manifold pressure is compared against 75% barometric pressure.

	brclr *b45_IPL1, #b45_TpsBadSignal, THROTTLESENSOR_OKAY    ; branch if bit(s) clear
	ldaa Temp0	    ; load a with memory contents
	cmpa RVLSPD_CarSpeedForRevLimitWithTBOff    ; compare a with memory contents (data is 14)
	bcc  L1484	    ; branch if greater or equal
	bra  L1483	    ; branch

* **Stage IV Setting**: Retained at 20 counts (10 mph) in Stage IV calibrations.

SCNVHI.overview: SCNVHI defines the upper gear ratio threshold for manual transmission clutch pedal disengagement and clutch slip detection. On manual transmission vehicles, depressing the clutch pedal or suffering clutch slippage disconnects engine speed from wheel speed, allowing the engine to free-rev if the cruise servo continues pulling the throttle open. The engine controller monitors the ratio of vehicle road speed to distributor pulse period. When the clutch is engaged in high gear, this product remains within a defined mechanical gear ratio window. If the clutch pedal is pressed or the clutch slips, engine RPM flares, causing the calculated product to spike past SCNVHI and instantly disengaging cruise control.
SCNVHI.overview_markdown:
`SCNVHI` defines the upper gear ratio threshold for manual transmission clutch pedal disengagement and clutch slip detection.

On manual transmission vehicles, depressing the clutch pedal or suffering clutch slippage disconnects engine speed from wheel speed, allowing the engine to free-rev if the cruise servo continues pulling the throttle open. The engine controller monitors the ratio of vehicle road speed to distributor pulse period. When the clutch is engaged in high gear, this product remains within a defined mechanical gear ratio window. If the clutch pedal is pressed or the clutch slips, engine RPM flares, causing the calculated product to spike past `SCNVHI` and instantly disengaging cruise control.
SCNVHI.tuners_guide: SCNVHI is a vital safety setting for manual transmission vehicles that lack a dedicated clutch pedal cruise cutout switch. If installing custom transmission gear sets, non-factory final drive ratios, or significantly different tire diameters, calculate the resulting speed-to-RPM product in top gear to ensure it does not exceed SCNVHI during normal cruising. Setting SCNVHI too low results in false cruise dropouts during highway cruising. Setting SCNVHI to 255 counts widens the upper threshold, which is standard in Stage IV calibrations.
SCNVHI.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Clutch Slip & Shift Protection**:
  * Automatically drops out of cruise control when driver presses the clutch pedal or if clutch disc slips under boost.
  * Prevents engine free-revving flare when clutch is disengaged without brake pedal touch.
* **Gear Ratio / Tire Changes**:
  * After changing transmission final drive or tire diameter, verify top gear ratio product remains below `SCNVHI`.
* **Stage IV Calibration Setting**:
  * Factory 2.5L calibration uses 241 counts; Stage IV calibrations set `SCNVHI` to 255 counts for maximum ratio tolerance.
SCNVHI.operating_conditions:
* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `CruiseResumeSwitchPressed` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:8530-8531`), called from `ControlCruiseServo0_MM` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:8473-8986`).
* **Gating Conditions**:
  * Manual transmission vehicle (`CONFIG_ConfigurationFlags` bit `cfg_ATX` clear at line 8498).
  * Engine running with no distributor pulse timer overflows.
* **Math & Branch**:
  * Multiplies vehicle speed `Temp0` by distributor pulse period `DistributorFallingEdgePulsewidth_HB`.
  * Scales product by 17 via `ScaleYbyA` at line 8525.
  * Compares product against `SCNVHI` at line 8530; if higher or equal (`bcc DropOutOfCruise`), execution jumps to disengage cruise.

Vehicle speed `Temp0` is multiplied by distributor period `DistributorFallingEdgePulsewidth_HB` at line 8521. Line 8525 calls `ScaleYbyA` with constant 17. The resulting scaled gear ratio is loaded into accumulator B at line 8529. At line 8530, `cmpb SCNVHI_CruiseControlForBrakeFlagManualTransmissionClutchDisable` tests the ratio. If carry is clear (`bcc DropOutOfCruise`), indicating the ratio meets or exceeds `SCNVHI`, cruise disengages immediately.

	beq  L1719	    ; branch if equal (zero)
	ldab #0xff	    ; load b with value -11111111-
L1719:	cmpb SCNVHI_CruiseControlForBrakeFlagManualTransmissionClutchDisable	; compare b with memory contents (data is ff)
	bcc  DropOutOfCruise	; branch if greater or equal
	cmpb SCNVLO_CruiseControlForBrakeFlagManualTransmissionClutchDisable	; compare b with memory contents (data is 52)
	bcs  DropOutOfCruise	; branch if lower

* **Companion Boundary**: Paired directly with lower gear ratio boundary `SCNVLO_CruiseControlForBrakeFlagManualTransmissionClutchDisable`.

SCNVLO.overview: SCNVLO defines the lower gear ratio threshold for manual transmission clutch disengagement and downshift cutout detection. In manual transmission Chrysler vehicles, cruise control is intended to operate in 4th or 5th gear. If the driver downshifts to 2nd or 3rd gear without touching the brake, or if the clutch pedal is partially depressed, engine RPM rises relative to vehicle speed, driving the calculated speed-to-RPM product downward. If the ratio drops below SCNVLO, the engine controller detects that the transmission is no longer operating in an approved high gear and immediately disengages cruise control.
SCNVLO.overview_markdown:
`SCNVLO` defines the lower gear ratio threshold for manual transmission clutch disengagement and downshift cutout detection.

In manual transmission Chrysler vehicles, cruise control is intended to operate in 4th or 5th gear. If the driver downshifts to 2nd or 3rd gear without touching the brake, or if the clutch pedal is partially depressed, engine RPM rises relative to vehicle speed, driving the calculated speed-to-RPM product downward. If the ratio drops below `SCNVLO`, the engine controller detects that the transmission is no longer operating in an approved high gear and immediately disengages cruise control.
SCNVLO.tuners_guide: Retain the factory setting of 82 counts for stock manual transaxles (A520, A523, A555, A568). If swapping transaxles or installing custom close-ratio gear sets where 4th gear produces a lower speed-to-RPM product, verify that the calculated ratio in 4th gear remains safely above SCNVLO. If cruise drops out unexpectedly upon shifting into 4th gear, lower SCNVLO to 65 or 70 counts to accommodate the shorter gear ratio.
SCNVLO.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Downshift Lockout**:
  * Disengages cruise control if the driver downshifts to lower gears without pressing the brake pedal.
  * Enforces cruise operation strictly in high cruising gears (4th and 5th gear).
* **Transaxle Swaps**:
  * When converting to short final drive ratios (such as 3.87 or 4.05 gearing), verify the 4th gear ratio product does not drop below `SCNVLO`.
* **Companion Parameter**:
  * Forms the lower bound of the manual transmission ratio window, with `SCNVHI` forming the upper bound.

* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `CruiseResumeSwitchPressed` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:8532-8533`), called from `ControlCruiseServo0_MM` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:8473-8986`).
* **Gating Conditions**:
  * Manual transmission vehicle (`cfg_ATX` clear).
  * Ratio product passed upper check (`ratio < SCNVHI`).
* **Comparison & Branch**:
  * Compares calculated gear ratio in accumulator B against `SCNVLO` via `cmpb SCNVLO` at line 8532.
  * If lower (`bcs DropOutOfCruise`), execution jumps to disengage cruise immediately.

SCRMP1.overview: SCRMP1 (SecondaryRampSubtractor1) establishes the closed-loop oxygen sensor toggle duration modifier used specifically while Phase 2 of the Exhaust Gas Recirculation diagnostic verification routine is active. In normal closed-loop operation, the engine controller looks up secondary ramp timing from a 2D table to pace how rapidly the oxygen sensor feedback counter toggles rich and lean. However, during Phase 2 EGR flow verification, the controller needs heightened sensitivity to detect the rapid exhaust gas composition change when the EGR valve shuts off. At line 3201 in the secondary ramp handler, if Phase 2 is active, the controller subtracts SCRMP1 from the toggle timer instead of the standard table lookup value. The factory setting of 2 counts accelerates the oxygen sensor switching rate, ensuring rapid feedback response during the diagnostic test.
SCRMP1.overview_markdown:
`SCRMP1` (SecondaryRampSubtractor1) establishes the closed-loop oxygen sensor toggle duration modifier used specifically while Phase 2 of the Exhaust Gas Recirculation diagnostic verification routine is active.

In normal closed-loop operation, the engine controller looks up secondary ramp timing from a 2D table to pace how rapidly the oxygen sensor feedback counter toggles rich and lean. However, during Phase 2 EGR flow verification, the controller needs heightened sensitivity to detect the rapid exhaust gas composition change when the EGR valve shuts off.

At line 3201 in the secondary ramp handler, if Phase 2 is active, the controller subtracts `SCRMP1` from the toggle timer instead of the standard table lookup value. The factory setting of 2 counts accelerates the oxygen sensor switching rate, ensuring rapid feedback response during the diagnostic test.
SCRMP1.tuners_guide: Raising SCRMP1 subtracts a larger value from the oxygen sensor toggle duration timer, causing the closed-loop system to switch and step its integrator more rapidly while the EGR flow test is underway. This can help sluggish narrowband oxygen sensors keep up with the diagnostic sequence. Lowering SCRMP1 to 1 or 0 slows down closed-loop feedback integration during Phase 2, which may smooth out fuel trim jitter on vehicles with large injectors. Setting SCRMP1 to its factory setting of 2 counts preserves the original closed-loop response calibration.
SCRMP1.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Raising SCRMP1**: Accelerates the closed-loop oxygen sensor toggle rate during Phase 2 testing, improving detection speed on older or slower-responding narrowband sensors.
* **Lowering SCRMP1**: Slows down the closed-loop integrator adjustment rate during Phase 2. Useful on modified engines with large fuel injectors to avoid overshooting stoichiometric fueling during the test.
* **EGR Diagnostic Cross-Coupling**: Directly linked to `EGRVar2` bit 7; has no effect during normal driving outside of active Phase 2 flow verification.
* **Factory Calibration**: 2 counts provides an optimal balance between fast transient detection and closed-loop fuel stability.
SCRMP1.operating_conditions:
* **Enclosing Routine**: `WorkWithSecondaryRamp` (lines 3195–3207), specifically at line 3201.
* **Called From**: `ModifyO2FeedbackCountVarToMaintainStoich_MM` (line 3190).
* **Precondition Flag**: Bit 7 of `EGRVar2` set (`brclr *EGRVar2, #bit_bit7, L1226` falls through to line 3201).
* **Calculation**: `Timer_O2ToggleDuration - SCRMP1_SecondaryRampSubtractor1` evaluated in accumulator A.
* **Branch Behavior**: Always executes `bra L1227` to check for toggle duration expiration (`bcc O2_SensorStuckOnOneSideTooLong`).

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In subroutine `WorkWithSecondaryRamp`, after looking up the ramp cell, line 3199 loads `Timer_O2ToggleDuration` into accumulator A. Line 3200 tests bit 7 of `EGRVar2` (`brclr *EGRVar2, #bit_bit7, L1226`). During normal driving, bit 7 is clear, branching to `L1226` to subtract the standard table value B (`sba`). However, when Phase 2 EGR diagnostic testing is active, bit 7 is set; execution falls into line 3201, which executes `suba SCRMP1_SecondaryRampSubtractor1` (factory 0x02 = 2 counts). Line 3202 branches via `bra L1227` to line 3205 (`bcc O2_SensorStuckOnOneSideTooLong`), evaluating whether the toggle timer has expired and advancing the closed-loop fuel feedback integrator.

; --- WorkWithSecondaryRamp (T-SMEC_v19.asm:3195-3207) ---
WorkWithSecondaryRamp:
	ldx  #SECRMP_SecondaryRamp    ; load index with value
	bsr  DetermineRampCellFromRPMandMAP    ; call subroutine
	sei		    ; disable interrupts
	ldaa Timer_O2ToggleDuration    ; load a with memory contents
	brclr *EGRVar2, #bit_bit7, L1226	; branch if bit(s) clear
	suba SCRMP1_SecondaryRampSubtractor1	;  (data is 02)
	bra  L1227	    ; branch

L1226:	sba		    ; (Timer_O2Toggle - limit value)
L1227:	bcc  O2_SensorStuckOnOneSideTooLong    ; branch if the timer is greater than the limit value, timer expired
	cli		    ; enable interrupts
	rts		    ; return from subroutine

* **Subsystem Bridge**: Forms a direct control linkage between the EGR diagnostic monitor and the primary closed-loop O2 feedback routine.
* **Subtractor Arithmetic**: Replaces table lookup subtraction with a fixed scalar subtraction of 2 counts when Phase 2 is running.

SCRMP1.raw_text: OVERVIEW: SCRMP1 (SecondaryRampSubtractor1) establishes the closed-loop oxygen sensor toggle duration modifier used specifically while Phase 2 of the Exhaust Gas Recirculation diagnostic verification routine is active. In normal closed-loop operation, the engine controller looks up secondary ramp timing from a 2D table to pace how rapidly the oxygen sensor feedback counter toggles rich and lean. However, during Phase 2 EGR flow verification, the controller needs heightened sensitivity to detect the rapid exhaust gas composition change when the EGR valve shuts off. At line 3201 in the secondary ramp handler, if Phase 2 is active, the controller subtracts SCRMP1 from the toggle timer instead of the standard table lookup value. The factory setting of 2 counts accelerates the oxygen sensor switching rate, ensuring rapid feedback response during the diagnostic test. | TUNER'S GUIDE: Raising SCRMP1 subtracts a larger value from the oxygen sensor toggle duration timer, causing the closed-loop system to switch and step its integrator more rapidly while the EGR flow test is underway. This can help sluggish narrowband oxygen sensors keep up with the diagnostic sequence. Lowering SCRMP1 to 1 or 0 slows down closed-loop feedback integration during Phase 2, which may smooth out fuel trim jitter on vehicles with large injectors. Setting SCRMP1 to its factory setting of 2 counts preserves the original closed-loop response calibration.

SECRMP.overview: SECRMP is a specialized 22-word secondary ramp rate table that functions as a closed-loop recovery failsafe when the oxygen sensor remains on one side (rich or lean) longer than expected. While PRIRMP handles smooth incremental corrections during normal switching, SECRMP activates when Timer_O2ToggleDuration exceeds the calibrated cell timeout limit, applying aggressive secondary fuel kicks to rapidly drive the mixture back toward stoichiometric. SECRMP defines the RPM and MAP grid boundaries, the secondary kick values (with lean corrections represented in two's complement format), and the duration limits for each operating cell.
SECRMP.overview_markdown:
`SECRMP` is a specialized 22-word secondary ramp rate table that functions as a closed-loop recovery failsafe when the oxygen sensor remains on one side (rich or lean) longer than expected.

While `PRIRMP` handles smooth incremental corrections during normal switching, `SECRMP` activates when `Timer_O2ToggleDuration` exceeds the calibrated cell timeout limit, applying aggressive secondary fuel kicks to rapidly drive the mixture back toward stoichiometric.

`SECRMP` defines the RPM and MAP grid boundaries, the secondary kick values (with lean corrections represented in two's complement format), and the duration limits for each operating cell.
SECRMP.tuners_guide: Tuning SECRMP controls the aggression of the closed-loop recovery system. When tuning modified engines with aftermarket cams or delayed exhaust transit times, aggressive secondary ramp kicks can cause dramatic fuel swings and noticeable surging as the ECU violently overcorrects a delayed sensor signal. Softening the secondary kick values in SECRMP produces much smoother recovery without abrupt fuel surges. Lengthening the duration limits allows more time for normal primary ramp switching before secondary intervention occurs.
SECRMP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Mitigating Surging on Cammed Engines**:
  * Aggressive secondary kicks can cause harsh surging when an exhaust sensor is slow to respond. Softening kick values in `SECRMP` eliminates abrupt overcorrections.
* **Recovery Failsafe**:
  * Operates only when the oxygen sensor has failed to toggle across the stoichiometric threshold within the cell's duration limit.
* **Two's Complement Lean Kicks**:
  * Rich kicks are positive values; lean kicks are stored as negative two's complement signed values.
* **Companion Constants**:
  * Interacts with `SCRMP1` and `SCRMP2` subtractor constants during timer evaluation.
SECRMP.operating_conditions:
* **Enclosing Subroutine**: `WorkWithSecondaryRamp` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:3195-3212`), instruction line 3196.
* **Gating Conditions**: Closed loop active (`b4f_O2Valid` set, `b50_StayOpenLoop` clear), and primary ramp has not toggled.
* **Comparison & Branch Polarity**:
  * Line 3196 loads index register X with `#SECRMP_SecondaryRamp`.
  * `DetermineRampCellFromRPMandMAP` selects the active cell.
  * Line 3199 loads `Timer_O2ToggleDuration` into register A.
  * Evaluates timeout limit; if timer expired (`bcc O2_SensorStuckOnOneSideTooLong`), secondary ramp kick is loaded and applied.

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In `WorkWithSecondaryRamp`, line 3196 loads index register X with `#SECRMP_SecondaryRamp`. Line 3197 calls `DetermineRampCellFromRPMandMAP` to index the table. At line 3199, `ldaa Timer_O2ToggleDuration` loads elapsed toggle time. Lines 3200-3204 subtract the cell timeout limit (and `SCRMP1` if EGR active). If carry is clear (`bcc O2_SensorStuckOnOneSideTooLong`), the timer has expired. Line 3210 resets `Timer_O2ToggleDuration`, line 3212 loads the secondary ramp step from `0x00,x`, and execution falls into `PriAndSecRamp_IncrementO2SensorFeedbackCount` at line 3213 to force fuel correction.
technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
; --- WorkWithSecondaryRamp (T-SMEC_v19.asm:3195-3212) ---
WorkWithSecondaryRamp:
	ldx  #SECRMP_SecondaryRamp    ; load index with value
	bsr  DetermineRampCellFromRPMandMAP    ; call subroutine
	sei		    ; disable interrupts
	ldaa Timer_O2ToggleDuration    ; load a with memory contents
	brclr *EGRVar2, #bit_bit7, L1226	; branch if bit(s) clear
	suba SCRMP1_SecondaryRampSubtractor1	;  (data is 02)
	bra  L1227	    ; branch

L1226:	sba		    ; (Timer_O2Toggle - limit value)
L1227:	bcc  O2_SensorStuckOnOneSideTooLong    ; branch if the timer is greater than the limit value, timer expired
	cli		    ; enable interrupts
	rts		    ; return from subroutine

O2_SensorStuckOnOneSideTooLong:
	staa Timer_O2ToggleDuration    ; store a into memory
	cli		    ; enable interrupts
	ldaa 0x00,x	    ; load a with ramp value

SECRMP.calibration_notes:
* **Table Structure (Type 11)**:
  * Word 1: RPM Low / High boundary (0x293F).
  * Word 2: MAP Low / High boundary (0x335E).
  * Words 3-11: Cruise Cells 0-8 Secondary Ramp Steps (Rich high byte, Lean signed low byte).
  * Word 12: Idle Cell Secondary Ramp Step.
  * Words 13-21: Cruise Cells 0-8 Duration Timeout Limits.
  * Word 22: Idle Cell Duration Timeout Limit.
* **Companion Parameters**: Works with `SCRMP1` (secondary ramp subtractor) and `PRIRMP`.
* **Persistence**: Triggered dynamically by RAM timer `Timer_O2ToggleDuration`.

SETDLT.overview: SETDLT defines the calibration offset bias added to speed error during evaluation of the throttle cable adaptive delta variable. In Chrysler SMEC engine management, the cruise controller continuously monitors mechanical throttle linkage compliance and cable stretch by calculating the difference between commanded speed and measured vehicle velocity. SETDLT is added to this delta, allowing calibrators to introduce an intentional bias into the cable compensation routine. In factory calibrations, SETDLT is configured to 0 counts, providing pure symmetrical calculation.
SETDLT.overview_markdown:
`SETDLT` defines the calibration offset bias added to speed error during evaluation of the throttle cable adaptive delta variable.

In Chrysler SMEC engine management, the cruise controller continuously monitors mechanical throttle linkage compliance and cable stretch by calculating the difference between commanded speed and measured vehicle velocity. `SETDLT` is added to this delta, allowing calibrators to introduce an intentional bias into the cable compensation routine. In factory calibrations, `SETDLT` is configured to 0 counts, providing pure symmetrical calculation.
SETDLT.tuners_guide: Retain the factory setting of 0 counts in all standard vehicle applications. Introducing positive or negative bias with SETDLT alters the learned cable slack compensation variable, which can lead to steady-state speed offset errors where the vehicle settles 1 to 2 miles per hour above or below the commanded target setpoint.
SETDLT.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Symmetrical Error Baseline**:
  * Factory 0 counts provides unbiased calculation of throttle cable slack.
* **Linkage Compliance Compensation**:
  * Offset feeds into `CruiseControlVar6`, which tracks mechanical hysteresis in the throttle linkage.
* **Offset Errors**:
  * Non-zero values induce persistent steady-state speed offsets; keep at 0 counts.
SETDLT.operating_conditions:
* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `CalculateVehicleSpeed` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:8792-8798`), called from `ControlCruiseServo0_MM` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:8473-8986`).
* **Gating Conditions**:
  * Evaluated when `Counter_Cruise < CRSCN1`.
  * Compares scaled `CruiseSpeedSetpoint` against `VehicleSpeed_HB`.
* **Math & Application**:
  * Computes `(CruiseSpeedSetpoint * 4) - (VehicleSpeed_HB / 8)`.
  * Adds `SETDLT` via `adda SETDLT` at line 8796.
  * Updates adaptive variable `CruiseControlVar6`.

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In `CalculateVehicleSpeed` at line 8788, `VehicleSpeed_HB` is shifted right three times. Line 8792 loads `CruiseSpeedSetpoint` and shifts left twice (`lsla; lsla`), multiplying by 4. Line 8795 subtracts road speed via `sba`. At line 8796, `adda SETDLT_CruiseControlSetDeltaControlPointForCableAdaptive` adds the offset constant. If the resulting delta exceeds existing adaptive variable `CruiseControlVar6`, line 8804 stores accumulator A into `CruiseControlVar6`.
technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
; --- CalculateVehicleSpeed (T-SMEC_v19.asm:8792-8798) ---
	ldaa CruiseSpeedSetpoint    ; load a with memory contents
	lsla		    ; logical shift left a
	lsla		    ; logical shift left a
	sba		    ; subtract (a=a-b)
	adda SETDLT_CruiseControlSetDeltaControlPointForCableAdaptive	 ;  (data is 00)
	bmi  L1767	    ; branch if minus(hi bit 1)

SETDLT.calibration_notes:
* **Adaptive Variable Feed**: Directly updates `CruiseControlVar6` (learned cable slack delta).
* **Mathematical Form**: Delta = `(Setpoint * 4) - (Speed / 8) + SETDLT`.
* **Companion Parameter**: Coordinates with deadband constant `CRSCN2`.

SETIM1.overview: SETIM1 defines the upper timer qualification boundary paired with SETIME to establish a precise deceleration pulse suppression window. When the driver presses the coast switch, the deceleration timer increments. If the switch is held long enough to exceed SETIME but released before exceeding SETIM1, the controller recognizes a deliberate moderate coast event and sets status flags to prevent setup pulse lurching. If the switch is held beyond SETIM1, the timer transitions to extended deceleration mode. In factory calibrations, SETIM1 is set to 82 counts, representing approximately 0.91 seconds.
SETIM1.overview_markdown:
`SETIM1` defines the upper timer qualification boundary paired with `SETIME` to establish a precise deceleration pulse suppression window.

When the driver presses the coast switch, the deceleration timer increments. If the switch is held long enough to exceed `SETIME` but released before exceeding `SETIM1`, the controller recognizes a deliberate moderate coast event and sets status flags to prevent setup pulse lurching. If the switch is held beyond `SETIM1`, the timer transitions to extended deceleration mode. In factory calibrations, `SETIM1` is set to 82 counts, representing approximately 0.91 seconds.
SETIM1.tuners_guide: SETIM1 governs the transition between moderate coast-down and extended coasting. Retain the factory value of 82 counts in virtually all calibrations. Modifying SETIM1 is only warranted if aftermarket steering wheel cruise controls or custom digital cruise stalks exhibit switch contact bounce or unusual button-hold resistance characteristics.
SETIM1.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Decel Window Boundary**:
  * Works with `SETIME` to define the timed window between 0.61 and 0.91 seconds for coast qualification.
  * Prevents contact bounce or erratic button presses from corrupting cruise state logic.
* **Extended Coast Transition**:
  * Once `Timer_CruiseDecelerate` exceeds `SETIM1`, bit 2 of `CruiseStatus` is cleared (`anda #~b2f_bit2`), returning the state machine to normal switch tracking.
* **Factory Value**:
  * Calibrated to 82 counts in stock calibrations; keep stock for standard Chrysler cruise stalks.
SETIM1.operating_conditions:
* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `ContinueCruise` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:8586-8592`), called from `ControlCruiseServo0_MM` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:8473-8986`).
* **Gating Conditions**:
  * Evaluated only when `Timer_CruiseDecelerate >= SETIME`.
  * Switch inputs mirrored in `StartupSwitchMirror2`.
* **Comparison & Branch**:
  * Compares `Timer_CruiseDecelerate` against `SETIM1` via `cmpb SETIM1` at line 8586.
  * If lower (`bcs`), sets bit 2 of `CruiseStatus` (`oraa #b2f_bit2`) and clears bits 0 and 1.
  * If higher or equal (`bcc L1728`), clears bit 2 (`anda #~b2f_bit2`).

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In `ContinueCruise` at line 8586, accumulator B holds `Timer_CruiseDecelerate` and executes `cmpb SETIM1_CruiseControlNoSetupPulseWhenDecelTimerBelowThis`. If borrow occurs (timer < `SETIM1`), execution falls through to line 8588; if bit 7 of `CruiseStatus` is clear, line 8589 asserts bit 2 (`oraa #b2f_bit2`) and clears bits 0 and 1. If timer >= `SETIM1`, execution branches to line 8592 (`L1728`) executing `anda #~b2f_bit2` to clear the decel setup inhibit flag.
technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
; --- ContinueCruise (T-SMEC_v19.asm:8586-8592) ---
	cmpb SETIM1_CruiseControlNoSetupPulseWhenDecelTimerBelowThis	; compare b with memory contents (data is 52)
	bcc  L1728	    ; branch if greater or equal
	brset *CruiseStatus, #bit_bit7, L1730	 ; branch if bit(s) set
	oraa #b2f_bit2	    ;  -00000100-
	anda #~(b2f_bit0 | b2f_bit1)
	bra  L1729
L1728:	anda #~b2f_bit2	    ; AND a with value -11111011-

SETIM1.calibration_notes:
* **Window Definition**: Active window span equals `SETIM1 - SETIME` = 82 - 55 = 27 counts (approx 0.30 seconds).
* **Flag Gating**: Manipulates bit 2 of `CruiseStatus`, which directly inhibits `CruiseBumpUpSpeedBy2Mph` setup pulse logic at line 8616.
* **Companion Parameter**: Must always be set higher than `SETIME_CruiseControlNoSetupPulseWhenDecelTimerAboveThis`.

SETIME.overview: SETIME defines the deceleration elapsed timer threshold for suppressing or modifying the vacuum setup pre-charge pulse when the driver releases the coast button. When holding down the coast or decelerate switch, the cruise servo vents and the vehicle slows down. Upon releasing the button, the driver intends to set a new, lower cruising speed. If the controller applied an aggressive vacuum pre-charge pulse immediately upon switch release, the vehicle would abruptly surge forward, causing an uncomfortable jerk. SETIME monitors the deceleration timer; if the button was held longer than SETIME, aggressive pre-charging is suppressed to ensure smooth engagement at the new lower speed.
SETIME.overview_markdown:
`SETIME` defines the deceleration elapsed timer threshold for suppressing or modifying the vacuum setup pre-charge pulse when the driver releases the coast button.

When holding down the coast or decelerate switch, the cruise servo vents and the vehicle slows down. Upon releasing the button, the driver intends to set a new, lower cruising speed. If the controller applied an aggressive vacuum pre-charge pulse immediately upon switch release, the vehicle would abruptly surge forward, causing an uncomfortable jerk. `SETIME` monitors the deceleration timer; if the button was held longer than `SETIME`, aggressive pre-charging is suppressed to ensure smooth engagement at the new lower speed.
SETIME.tuners_guide: The factory setting of 55 counts (approximately 0.61 seconds) provides balanced switch debounce and deceleration transition timing. If drivers report that brief taps of the coast button result in sluggish re-engagement, raising SETIME extends the window where standard setup pulses are permitted. Lowering SETIME suppresses setup pulses earlier in the coast cycle, which can be useful if the car tends to surge or lurch forward after short coast maneuvers. Retain stock values unless custom switch gear requires non-standard timing.
SETIME.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Coast-to-Set Behavior**:
  * Suppresses aggressive vacuum pre-charge when driver holds the coast button to decelerate.
  * Factory 55 counts (approx 0.61 seconds) ensures smooth handoff to the new lower speed setting.
* **Preventing Decel Surge**:
  * If releasing coast causes an immediate forward lurch, lower `SETIME` to suppress setup pulsing earlier.
* **Secondary Use in Speed Calculation**:
  * In `CalculateVehicleSpeed` (line 8842), if `Timer_CruiseDecelerate` exceeds `SETIME`, the servo commands continuous vent to maintain deceleration.
SETIME.operating_conditions:
* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `ContinueCruise` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:8584-8588`) and `CalculateVehicleSpeed` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:8841-8846`).
* **Gating Conditions**:
  * Evaluated when coast/resume switch is held or released.
  * `Timer_CruiseDecelerate` incremented each foreground loop pass while switch is active.
* **Comparison & Branch**:
  * In `ContinueCruise`, compares `Timer_CruiseDecelerate` against `SETIME` via `cmpb SETIME` at line 8584.
  * If lower (`bcs L1730`), leaves state unchanged; if higher, evaluates `SETIM1` and asserts bit 2 of `CruiseStatus`.
  * In `CalculateVehicleSpeed`, if timer exceeds `SETIME`, branches to force vent command 0x8F.

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In `ContinueCruise` at line 8584, `Timer_CruiseDecelerate` is compared against `SETIME_CruiseControlNoSetupPulseWhenDecelTimerAboveThis`. If lower (`bcs L1730`), execution skips setup pulse modification. If equal or higher, execution checks `SETIM1` at line 8586. If between `SETIME` and `SETIM1`, line 8589 sets bit 2 of `CruiseStatus` (`oraa #b2f_bit2`) to flag decel-active setpoint. In `CalculateVehicleSpeed` at line 8842, `cmpa SETIME` branches to force vent command 0x8F if the timer is still running.
technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
; --- ContinueCruise (T-SMEC_v19.asm:8583-8588) ---
L1727:	ldab Timer_CruiseDecelerate    ; load b with memory contents
	cmpb SETIME_CruiseControlNoSetupPulseWhenDecelTimerAboveThis	; compare b with memory contents (data is 37)
	bcs  L1730	    ; branch if lower
	cmpb SETIM1_CruiseControlNoSetupPulseWhenDecelTimerBelowThis	; compare b with memory contents (data is 52)
	bcc  L1728	    ; branch if greater or equal

SETIME.calibration_notes:
* **Dual Routine Reference**: Referenced at line 8584 (switch qualification) and line 8842 (vent command during active deceleration).
* **Timer Scaling**: Incremented once per 11-millisecond main loop pass, making 55 counts equal to approximately 0.61 seconds.
* **Companion Parameter**: Paired directly with `SETIM1_CruiseControlNoSetupPulseWhenDecelTimerBelowThis`.

SETPW.overview: SETPW defines the initial vacuum setup pulse duration applied to the cruise servo the instant the driver presses the set switch. Prior to engagement, the cruise servo diaphragm is fully vented to atmospheric pressure, and throttle position is maintained exclusively by the driver foot on the accelerator pedal. When set is pressed, the engine controller must pre-charge the servo bellows with engine vacuum to take over the mechanical throttle load before the driver lifts off the accelerator. SETPW scales this pre-charge pulse duration across vehicle road speed, ensuring a seamless, imperceptible handoff without a sudden deceleration dip or forward jerk.
SETPW.overview_markdown:
`SETPW` defines the initial vacuum setup pulse duration applied to the cruise servo the instant the driver presses the set switch.

Prior to engagement, the cruise servo diaphragm is fully vented to atmospheric pressure, and throttle position is maintained exclusively by the driver foot on the accelerator pedal. When set is pressed, the engine controller must pre-charge the servo bellows with engine vacuum to take over the mechanical throttle load before the driver lifts off the accelerator. `SETPW` scales this pre-charge pulse duration across vehicle road speed, ensuring a seamless, imperceptible handoff without a sudden deceleration dip or forward jerk.
SETPW.tuners_guide: If releasing the gas pedal immediately after pressing the set switch causes the vehicle to momentarily sag or lose 1 to 2 mph before the servo catches, increase SETPW at that speed range to command a longer pre-charge pulse. Conversely, if the vehicle surges forward with unintended acceleration or kicks the gas pedal against the driver foot upon setting cruise, decrease SETPW. Vehicles with heavy throttle return springs or stiff mechanical linkage require higher SETPW values to overcome return spring resistance during handoff.
SETPW.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Set-Speed Sag / Dip**:
  * If releasing the accelerator pedal right after hitting set causes the car to momentarily sag or lose 1 to 2 mph, increase `SETPW` at that speed.
  * Provides a longer initial vacuum pulse to build servo holding tension faster.
* **Set-Speed Surge / Pedal Kick**:
  * If the car surges forward with unexpected acceleration when tapping set, reduce `SETPW`.
  * Prevents over-charging the vacuum servo diaphragm before driver pedal lift-off.
* **Speed-Scaled Progression**:
  * Factory values scale from 0.49 seconds at 35 mph up to 0.94 seconds at 85 mph, compensating for higher aerodynamic load at highway velocities.
SETPW.operating_conditions:
* **Subroutine & Line Numbers**: `CruiseBumpUpSpeedBy2Mph` (`T-SMEC_v19.asm:8648-8653`), called from `ControlCruiseServo0_MM` at line 8620 when `sw2_CruiseSet` is pressed.
* **Gating Conditions**:
  * Cruise switch ON and road speed within valid boundaries (`MINSET <= Speed <= MAXSET`).
  * Set switch pressed (`sw2_CruiseSet` set in `StartupSwitchMirror2`).
  * Setup pulse not inhibited by deceleration timer (`Timer_CruiseDecelerate` within normal range).
* **Lookup Operation**:
  * `ldaa CruiseSpeedSetpoint` loads target road speed in 0.5 mph increments.
  * `ldx #SETPW_CruiseControlSetupPulseForSet_FromSpeed` loads table pointer.
  * Calls `Lookup4ByteTable` and clamps positive pulse in `Temp1`.

technical_mechanics.text: Inside `T-SMEC_v19.asm`: In `CruiseBumpUpSpeedBy2Mph` at line 8648, `CruiseSpeedSetpoint` is loaded into accumulator A. Line 8649 loads `#SETPW_CruiseControlSetupPulseForSet_FromSpeed` into index register X, and line 8650 calls `Lookup4ByteTable`. If the lookup result is negative, line 8652 clamps accumulator B to 127 counts (0x7F). Line 8653 saves accumulator B into `Temp1`. This base setup pulse is subsequently modulated by manifold pressure in `RESTBL`.
technical_mechanics.assembly_code:
; --- CruiseBumpUpSpeedBy2Mph (T-SMEC_v19.asm:8648-8653) ---
L1739:	ldaa CruiseSpeedSetpoint    ; load a with memory contents
	ldx  #SETPW_CruiseControlSetupPulseForSet_FromSpeed    ; load index with value
	jsr  Lookup4ByteTable	 ; call subroutine
	bpl  L1740	    ; branch if plus (hi bit 0)
	ldab #0x7f	    ; load b with value -01111111-
L1740:	stab Temp1	    ; store b into memory

SETPW.calibration_notes:
* **Multi-Stage Precharge**: The base pulse looked up from `SETPW` is stored into `Temp1` and immediately fed into `RESTBL` (manifold pressure correction) and `BitFlags_27` (adaptive learned trim).
* **Speed Unit Scaling**: The X-axis represents road speed where 70 counts corresponds to 35 mph, 130 counts corresponds to 65 mph, and 170 counts corresponds to 85 mph.
* **Companion Setting**: Works directly with `RESTBL` (vacuum correction) and `RESTBL2` (resume delta pulse).

SETUP.overview: SETUP stores a dedicated sixteen-bit diagnostic synchronization pattern within the calibration identification header. Configured to fifty-five AA in factory calibrations, this parameter establishes an alternating binary bit pattern of alternating zeros and ones. During automated factory test bench procedures and diagnostic interface initialization, automated test equipment reads this framing constant to verify serial bit alignment, baud rate synchronization, and data bus integrity before beginning high-speed calibration downloads or hardware verification.
SETUP.overview_markdown:
`SETUP` stores a dedicated sixteen-bit diagnostic synchronization pattern within the calibration identification header.

Configured to fifty-five AA in factory calibrations, this parameter establishes an alternating binary bit pattern of alternating zeros and ones. During automated factory test bench procedures and diagnostic interface initialization, automated test equipment reads this framing constant to verify serial bit alignment, baud rate synchronization, and data bus integrity before beginning high-speed calibration downloads or hardware verification.
SETUP.tuners_guide: SETUP should not be modified. It serves strictly as a communication alignment signature for diagnostic and manufacturing hardware. Modifying SETUP has zero effect on engine operation, vehicle drivability, or boost control, and will alter the calibration ROM checksum, requiring recalculation of the checksum fixup byte to prevent diagnostic fault code fifty-three.
SETUP.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Factory Synchronization Pattern**:
  * Configured to alternating binary bits to provide serial framing verification for diagnostic hardware.
* **Zero Engine Impact**:
